💡 Key Takeaways
  • Circan’s November 2025 video game sales report has easily been one of the most anticipated.
  • We’re talking, of course, about Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 the latest releases in their respective multiplayer shooter series.
  • Cricana’s report covers spending on video game software, hardware, and accessories in the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Circan’s November 2025 video game sales report has easily been one of the most anticipated. For one, November is always one of the most lucrative for the games industry, but this year in particular has seen several major hits - including upcoming entries in two rival series.

We’re talking, of course, about Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 the latest releases in their respective multiplayer shooter series. The decades-old fight to claim the top spot has long been won by Call of Duty, but the latest Battlefield has achieved what many thought was impossible.

Cricana’s report covers spending on video game software, hardware, and accessories in the U.S. November 2025 saw spending fall by 4% compared to November 2024, bringing in a total of $5.9 billion.

Industry observers note that software technically saw growth during the month, but declines in hardware, and accessories were mainly responsible for the drop in overall spending. Black Ops 7 continued Call of Duty’s 18-Year Streak in topping sales in its launch month.

However, this year’s game did not also top the year-to-date charts, something the series has done consistently, and more than any other top-selling game each year - with rare exceptions. Battlefield 6 is firmly in the lead there, cementing its claim as 2025’s best-selling title. Black Ops 7, fittingly, occupies in the #7 spot there.

Separately from the best-selling game title fight, November has actually been one of the worst for the industry in terms of hardware sales. The report notes that the three major platform holders - Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo have all seen their hardware sales decline.

Recent findings suggest that spending on hardware during November amounted to only $695 million, a massive 27% decline compared to November 2024. According to the report, that’s the worst dollar amount total for any November since 2005, when it comes to hardware specifically. All three current-gen consoles totaled 1.6 million units sold, which Circana also notes is the lowest for any November since 1995.

In a recent development, this all doesn’t bode especially well for the industry. November has always been a key holiday shopping month, but it’s clear the constantly rising console prices - and already high game prices - have had a big impact.

Final Fantasy 14's Evercold is Set to Be a Fascinating Social Experiment

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1904 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that with well over a decade now under its belt since its fateful “rebirth” in 2013, Final Fantasy XIV is one of the biggest second chance success stories in the gaming industry, and has since cemented its coveted spot in the ever-exclusive genre of MMORPGs.
  • Industry observers note that all that stated, the insane amount of changes that are coming to Final Fantasy 14 with Evercold’s release in February 2027 are by and large systemic in scale.
  • For years now and from one expansion to the next, the majority of Final Fantasy 14’s social circles have organically gravitated to the game’s biggest cities, turning them into bustling hubs of conversation and commerce that seldom ever sleep, no matter your timezone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that with well over a decade now under its belt since its fateful “rebirth” in 2013, Final Fantasy XIV is one of the biggest second chance success stories in the gaming industry, and has since cemented its coveted spot in the ever-exclusive genre of MMORPGs. While its battle gameplay remains a fixture of criticism, its player community only continues to grow and the Evercold expansion is set to bring about an avalanche of groundbreaking changes to alleviate many of those criticisms at long last (hopefully).

Industry observers note that all that stated, the insane amount of changes that are coming to Final Fantasy 14 with Evercold’s release in February 2027 are by and large systemic in scale. This means that the way players interact and how they socialize in the game will likely change, in ways that are both subtle and not so subtle. The ripple effect it will have is all but inevitable, and it remains to be seen how exactly it will all play out, not just for Evercold but for all expansions that follow it.

For years now and from one expansion to the next, the majority of Final Fantasy 14’s social circles have organically gravitated to the game’s biggest cities, turning them into bustling hubs of conversation and commerce that seldom ever sleep, no matter your timezone. By this I’m referring to New Gridania, Ul’dah, and Limsa Lominsa, the cities that first made their grand appearance in A Realm Reborn and have since remained the places that most players return to, regardless of what expansion they’re working through or whatever other type of content that’s keeping them busy.

Subsequent expansions have since debuted some truly vibrant city hubs, from the vast, enamoring architecture in Stormblood’s Kugane to the posh rooms of Shadowbringers’s Eulmore and later the futuristic storefronts of Dawntrail’s Solution 9. However, while these places see an initial surge in player counts that linger during their respective expansion’s patch cycle, as the content surrounding it wanes and periods of “content drought” come and go, nine times out of ten, players ultimately wind up back on the benches of Limsa Lominsa or the streets of Ul’dah to congregate with their fellow Warriors of Light.

In a recent development, while there’s no point blank reason for why this happens with every expansion, the easy answer is that all proverbial rivers always flow back to the cities that started it all. They’re where most of the game’s seasonal events take place, for instance, to allow “sprout” players to participate alongside years-long veterans. Free Companies, or FF14’s version of guilds, are often a mix of newcomers and seasoned players, and these cities are often where they mingle outside of their respective “FC House”.

Industry observers note that there’s the commerce side of things too, as Market Boards, which serve as the main point of contact for selling items to other players in the game, are plentiful and often only a few steps away from an aetheryte crystal teleporter. On top of that, vendors and other NPCs who teach combat, crafting, and gathering classes are easy to come by in these places, all making for a reliable hub to take care of whatever you need on the day-to-day while hanging out with your friends.

According to recent reports, however, this dynamic that’s remained in place all these years in FFXIV may experience a sort of social earthquake with Evercold’s arrival, as the game’s character UI is set to become almost entirely self-contained when it comes to progression and upgrades. The need to seek out vendors for everything is going to shrink dramatically (at least from what we’ve been told in the Fanfest keynotes so far), which takes a vital element for these active hubs out of the equation.

If players can take their tools of progression with them on the go instead of traveling to these sources, what will that mean for not only these cities but other hubs in the game that inevitably empty out in later patch cycles? Will places like Limsa Lominsa stand firm despite these changes or will they face winds of change that happen on a subconscious level? Most of all, what does that mean for late-expac hubs like Radz-at-Han and Solution 9? Will the dynamic of how hubs function in the game as a whole experience a generational shift?

This is by and far the biggest question Evercold faces, and it will be fascinating to watch that unfold in the initial months of the expansion’s content cycle.

According to recent reports, while the social dynamic of FF14 is potentially about to undergo its biggest evolution since the game’s inception, there is one systemic upgrade already underway that may help smooth over the impact that has. Director Naoki (“Yoshi-P”) Yoshida and his team have been in the process of integrating the game’s massive regional data centers, which house millions of players everywhere from North America to Europe, China, Japan, and Oceania.

Up to now, those data centers have helped mesh their respective servers to help give a sense of different global “neighborhoods” that players can feel at home in. However, as the game now has such a far reach, players have since proven that friendship has no boundaries, often teaming up with Warriors of Light in entirely different regions to do content or simply hang out.

Recent findings suggest that to get to another data center, however, the process was tedious to the point that it would feel even more isolating than it should have. Normally, you’d have to log out of the game entirely and facilitate a data center transfer from the log-in menu, which can take up to a few minutes. Then, if you want to jump to yet another data center that’s not your own from there, you'd have to log back out, return to your home data center, then facilitate yet another transfer to get there. Exhausting, to say the least.

It has been revealed that finally, though, that archaic process is steadily becoming history as now the NA region has merged its data centers with those in the EU, which allows players to effortlessly jump between both hubs from any main aetheryte in the game’s biggest cities. No more having to spend precious time logging out and transferring over and over. Now it’s a simple click at the aetheryte and you’re there in seconds.

Not only is this extraordinarily more convenient, such a merge is helping to dissolve that imposed isolation and help all of these “neighborhoods” feel closer together. Players no longer have to feel like they have to resort to certain servers to get the experience they want, and ultimately this could (hopefully) lead to more content participation balance across the board. That was technically the initial goal of these integrations according to Yoshi-P, to help alleviate duty queue times, but we’ll have to wait for long-term results to really get the substantial picture.

While so much of the game’s systemic infrastructure is getting a staggering rework for Evercold onward, one particular social feature in the game that continues to get the proverbial rug pull, sadly, is housing.

Yoshi-P did announce during the Tokyo Fanfest keynote that housing in the game is getting a budget expansion for even more plots, though they’re still actively exploring how to implement that in a more effective way that doesn’t strain the digital space they have for it. Whether that’s creating “hidden” plot areas or more districts remains to be seen, and we’ll have to wait until after Evercold’s debut to find out the result.

It has been revealed that while it’s always nice to have more room for players to settle and customize their home away from home, the hard truth is that FFXIV’s housing system remains an inconvenient mess with no indication of when we could potentially see the systemic change it so desperately needs. Over the years, the game has dealt with creating too much artificial scarcity for housing, turning it into far more of a privilege than it should be in a global MMORPG.

Recent findings suggest that it’s a glaring reality of how the game has chosen to approach housing from the get-go, and how those decisions have led it down a path that it can’t seem to escape or fix in an effective manner. Instead, it’s more plots to placate the masses, the option to manipulate the amount of interior space for an additional gil fee, and a long overdue unlock on the ability to “float” furnishings. These are nice additions, but I’ve long viewed FF14’s housing situation from the bigger picture.

Ultimately, I think it comes down to the desire to make housing genuinely feel like a neighborhood you can actively walk around in rather than making it entirely instanced like other games do. Trying to honor that immersion is commendable, but when it comes at the cost of depriving countless players of the opportunity to experience that based on a skewed luck system, then what is the point in the end?

It has been revealed that all that said, I’m not without the hope that things could still change in the future for housing. Rather, it could very well be that it needs its own expansion to pull it off, just as the game’s done with its graphic overhaul in Dawntrail and now the gameplay overhaul in Evercold. Or perhaps, this is the way it truly needs to be in Final Fantasy 14 in terms of the game’s social dynamic. Maybe losing our digital neighborhoods to instanced housing isn’t the answer. Whatever it could turn out to be, to truly strengthen the game’s social sphere, housing needs to be something attainable for everyone, not a privileged few.

It has been revealed that final Fantasy XIV’s combat has been an ongoing point of discussion, criticism, praise, and everything in between. However, in the years of Dawntrail’s patch cycle, the criticism reached a fever pitch in regards to the game’s growing lack of job identity and how stated jobs haven’t seen much of a systemic update at all since A Realm Reborn. It had gotten to the point that the future of FFXIV had reached a questionable stage, and that if these ongoing issues weren’t addressed then the MMO could see a tragic downturn sooner rather than later.

It has been revealed that with that, Evercold is set to bring about a slew of long-awaited changes to battle content, pretty much from top to bottom. Virtually every aspect of combat in the game is set to get some degree of change, along with entirely newly introduced additions such as the already widely praised Gauntlet of Power. Meanwhile, existing content such as Alliance Raids are getting dissected and reworked to hopefully better fit modern playstyles where time is more precious and content needs to be more inherently beneficial to players.

These changes are yet another factor in the equation that will undoubtedly affect how players will team up and work together in a post-Evercold setting versus the traditional methods that have driven the game for years. Having more flexibility in playstyle and more diversity in the types of battle content that are available are definitely net positives for FF14, and it will be interesting to see how that subsequently helps the social aspect of the game evolve in the months and years to come.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Suzuki left the U.S. car market in 2012, but it still builds the kind of small hatchbacks European buyers have long favored, now also powered by electricity. Its latest is the Ignis EV, a city car that measures just 11 feet 9 inches long (3.57 meters). It’s due in Europe in summer 2027, when it will face a upcoming generation of small EVs from both European and Chinese automakers.

The Ignis is Suzuki’s first subcompact electric car developed for global markets, but its roots are in Japan. The company recently introduced the e Sky there, an electric kei car that supplies the basis for the Ignis’s body and powertrain. The Ignis still has the typical kei proportions (it's tall and narrow), but Suzuki claims it took the car onto European city streets and winding roads to tune the suspension and power delivery, making it more appealing to the people it hopes will buy one.

A 26-kilowatt-hour lithium iron phosphate battery sits under the floor of Suzuki’s dedicated Heartect-e electric platform. Yes, that really is what it's called. Up front, the motor, inverter, and reduction gears share a single compact assembly that sends 90 horsepower and 98 pound-feet (133 Nm) to the front wheels. Suzuki indicates it chose LFP for safety and longevity, but it hasn’t given the European car a range or charging figure yet.

The Ignis EV has a very tight 29.5-foot (9-meter) turning circle. Its overhangs are tiny, giving it a wheel-at-each-corner stance that looks unique while maximizing available interior room. The LED signatures at both ends take their shape from digital numerals, and the dark pillars give the roof a floating look.

It has been revealed that inside, a curve runs from the dashboard into the doors, with a wide display and a ceramic-inspired storage tray across the dash. Suzuki President Toshihiro Suzuki credits the organization’s decades of building Japanese mini vehicles for its ability to provide a genuinely usable cabin in such a small footprint.

For decades, European brands had most of this business to themselves. If you wanted an inexpensive car that could squeeze down a narrow street, Fiat would happily sell you a Panda, Renault a Twingo and Volkswagen an Up. Chinese automakers see an opening as those buyers go electric.

Leapmotor brought the T03 to Europe through its partnership with Stellantis, while BYD adapted its Chinese-market Seagull for Europe and called it the Dolphin Surf. Driving the latter, what stood out to me was how well it drove, how little felt cheap, and how much kit it had for its sub-€20,000 starting price.

By the time the Ignis arrives next year, European buyers will have had plenty of practice shopping for small EVs. Renault has revived both the 5 and the Twingo as electric cars, and there’s also the related Dacia Spring. Volkswagen has the ID. Polo, Cupra has the Raval, and Skoda has the Epiq, and there definitely seems to be demand for them. In September, a major VW dealer group reported more than 30,000 orders for the ID. Polo and a waiting list stretching to ten months.

That leaves one big question for the little Suzuki. What will it cost? Consider the redesigned Dacia Spring. Dacia moved production from China to Slovenia, shared the electric Twingo’s underpinnings, and produced a car that starts at €17,900 in Italy. It gets up to 155 miles (250 kilometers) of WLTP range from a battery only slightly larger than the one in the Ignis.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The next EV to plug in at a ski resort might be the one that groomed your trail.
  • Under the agreement, Kässbohrer will connect its customers with ChargePoint for chargers, software, and support with planning, installation, and day-to-day operations.
  • Recent findings suggest that kässbohrer’s first fully electric groomer, the PistenBully 100 E, uses electric motors to move the machine and spin the tiller that smooths the snow.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The next EV to plug in at a ski resort might be the one that groomed your trail. ChargePoint has struck a deal with Kässbohrer, the German company behind PistenBully snow groomers, to bring charging to ski resorts and indoor ski facilities across Europe and North America.

Under the agreement, Kässbohrer will connect its customers with ChargePoint for chargers, software, and support with planning, installation, and day-to-day operations. Resorts can use the same provider for the snow groomers and other vehicles they keep at the maintenance depot, as well as for the EV chargers skiers use while they’re out on the slopes.

Recent findings suggest that kässbohrer’s first fully electric groomer, the PistenBully 100 E, uses electric motors to move the machine and spin the tiller that smooths the snow. It has a 196 kWh battery and can handle up to three hours of normal grooming on a charge, according to the manufacturer. It can take up to 22 kW on AC or 150 kW on a DC fast charger. Finally, HoYoverse is making it easier for players to jump into 2.5’s new story chapter using Advance Screening. Ye Shunguang and Zhao will be available for the entire patch’s duration, and reruns in the second half will guarantee another S-Rank.

Recent findings suggest that you’ll be able to pick from Alice, Soldier 0 – Anby, or Astra. Zhao will herself be available as a login bonus alongside 1,000 Polychromes, a fresh outfit for Jane, and more. Tech Report: 9 Best Tech Parodies in GTA 6

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1222 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the Grand Theft Auto series tends to be a parody of real life, with there being loads of satirical comedy woven throughout the many fibers of each game.
  • Tech plays a major role in the game, as you use your phone for many things, such as ordering a ride on the RydeMe app, or even bucking yourself using the aptly named BuckMe app.
  • You are going to be relying on a lot of tech companies throughout GTA 6, so it is obvious that there will be a number of jokes surrounding them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Grand Theft Auto series tends to be a parody of real life, with there being loads of satirical comedy woven throughout the many fibers of each game. This trend continues in Grand Theft Auto 6, with there being loads of hilarious parodies of well-known companies, television shows, radio broadcasts, and even tech.

Tech plays a major role in the game, as you use your phone for many things, such as ordering a ride on the RydeMe app, or even bucking yourself using the aptly named BuckMe app.

You are going to be relying on a lot of tech companies throughout GTA 6, so it is obvious that there will be a number of jokes surrounding them.

Texting plays a huge role in real life. After all, you text your friends, family members, and even coworkers about what is going on in your life. The same is done in GTA 6, and the game captures texting quite well, with both protagonists texting one another and various people about jobs.

While you may normally use the popular WhatsApp application to get your fill of communication, the people of GTA 6 use a slightly different app called WhatUp. This is a very obvious parody of WhatsApp, with a name that is almost identical.

Even the user interface is almost identical, with it featuring a very minimalist style showing the avatar or profile picture of each contact next to the messages.

Amazon is a go-to tech and shipping tech giant for many people nowadays. While we all may complain about capitalism, there is no denying the convenience of having everything at your fingertips through the use of an app that has next-day shipping.

According to recent reports, in GTA, the citizens of Leonida are using a slightly different company that is a clear parody of Amazon, and it is called Sahara. You can find boxes scattered around that mimic the exact shipping tape used by the company, the logo is very similar, and there is even Sahara Mirage, which is meant to be a parody of Amazon Prime.

Money makes the world go ‘round in real life, and it especially makes the world go ‘round in GTA 6. You are on a constant mission to collect money in the game, which in a way mimics real life. Anyway when you are handling money in real life, you might use a banking app, or you might use CashApp or Venmo.

GTA 6 has an app that parodies these real-life tools and it is called BuckMe - a hilarious name that has various uses, such as when you give yourself money, which is called bucking yourself.

This app is the go-to banking app that you get at the start of the game because you can’t afford to open a real checking account and it is just perfect.

In a recent development, did you know that you can play games within GTA 6? Odds are you probably did, and it is thanks to Cal. He so graciously installs the latest JoyStation in Jason’s home early in the game, allowing you to catch up on your gaming within your game.

The JoyStation is an obvious parody of the PlayStation 5, with the console looking almost identical to the real-life system you are probably playing GTA 6 on. Even the user interface looks extremely close to the real-life version.

The console isn’t just for looks, as it can be used to play some real games, with some of them even being easter eggs for real-life movies and games.

Industry observers note that when you need to get around the city in real life, you either rely on your car to get you from point A to point B, or you rely on someone else’s car. This can come in the form of a ride that you hire via a rideshare app like Lyft or Uber.

Just like in real life, you can get from point to point in GTA 6 by using the convenient ridesharing app aptly called RydeMe. It even comes complete with a Y instead of an I so you know it was made by the tech bros in Silicon Valley.

The app is great, as it lets you fast travel around the city. If only you could skip the unwanted conversation with the driver in real life. At least the prices match up with the inflated real-life equivalent.

Doomscrolling has become the norm lately, as apps like YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok all offer short-form content that you can easily digest and swipe away. Luckily, GTA 6 hasn’t gone that far… yet.

In a recent development, while you can’t doomscroll reels in GTA 6, you can flip through tons of posts thanks to the improved Snapmatic app. This app made an appearance in GTA 5, as it was used to take pictures.

Sources indicate that now, you can use it to scroll through countless posts about how we got something else before RAC 7. You can even read the comments, and those are something else entirely, so be prepared.

Industry observers note that dating in real life has been boiled down to a few different dating apps, but if you are looking to hook up with someone, you are probably going to use Tinder. Of course, you could try FarmersOnly, but to each their own.

In a recent development, sadly, you can’t get the experience of using a dating app in GTA 6, but you can help out Cal. Early in the game, you get to see the in-game version of Tinder, as Cal hands you his phone and you get to swipe right or left on various dating profiles.

The app is pretty accurate to the real-life equivalent, complete with cringy profiles, horrible pictures, and people with way too high of standards.

Industry observers note that there has been a rise of people who are vaping, and as someone who used to vape all the time, it is sad to see how much it has grown at times. Vaping has infected the world of Leonida as well, but one in particular that is worth pointing out is Manifestick.

This hilarious parody is meant to replace anxiety pens and mock those who wear a vape on a leash around their neck, as there are women who use them like they are addicted to them.

Oh wait, that is because they are addicted. You can discover that these vape pens are laced with cocaine, making them not so friendly and very addictive like the real-life nicotine infused sticks.

It has been revealed that cryptocurrency is everywhere nowadays. There are people who swear on Bitcoin, and we see a meme coin pop up almost every day. We have all heard stories of people being scammed because someone did a rug pull.

According to recent reports, throughout the game, you will interact with a manufacturer called AudaCity, and there is even a character named Papa Audacity. This company is creating DacityCoin, and you are meant to promote it with Redbull-style stunts that push the coin’s value up.

The protagonists even call out how the coin is a scam, but that doesn’t mean you can’t get in on the ground floor and be one of the few who profits off of everyone else’s losses.

#120943. Depression may be an early warning sign of Alzheimer's disease

Depression may be an early warning sign of Alzheimer's disease

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (546 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Changes in mood later in life may offer important clues about what is happening inside the brain, even before problems with memory or thinking become noticeable.
  • In a recent development, the study, published in JNeurosci, was conducted by Teodora Markova of Brandeis University and her colleagues.
  • Alzheimer's Protein Linked to Worsening Depression.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Changes in mood later in life may offer important clues about what is happening inside the brain, even before problems with memory or thinking become noticeable. Latest research suggests that the buildup of tau, a protein closely associated with Alzheimer's disease, may contribute to worsening depressive symptoms in older adults.

In a recent development, the study, published in JNeurosci, was conducted by Teodora Markova of Brandeis University and her colleagues. The team investigated how tau levels relate to depression during normal aging and in people experiencing the cognitive (memory, attention, and thinking) difficulties associated with Alzheimer's disease.

Alzheimer's Protein Linked to Worsening Depression.

To investigate this connection, researchers analyzed information from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, a research project that tracks changes in brain health over time. The data included older men and women, some with cognitive difficulties and others whose memory and thinking abilities remained intact.

According to recent reports, participants underwent multiple brain scans designed to detect tau accumulation and completed questionnaires assessing depressive symptoms at different points during the study. This allowed researchers to examine how changes in tau levels corresponded with changes in mood over time.

Sources indicate that among participants with normal cognitive abilities, the researchers discovered a striking pattern. Those whose tau levels increased more rapidly also tended to experience a faster rise in depressive symptoms. Higher tau levels also helped predict more severe depressive symptoms in these individuals.

The results suggest that tau may begin influencing mood before measurable cognitive problems emerge. However, the same relationships were not observed among participants who already had mild cognitive impairment or Alzheimer's disease.

Could Depression Reveal Early Brain Changes?

The findings suggest that tau accumulation during the early stages of brain aging may contribute to the development or worsening of depression. They also raise the possibility that changes in mood could provide useful information about brain health before memory loss becomes apparent.

In a recent development, researchers believe that following depressive symptoms over time, alongside other assessments, could eventually help identify older adults who may be at greater risk of developing neurodegenerative diseases. However, additional research is needed to establish whether these early changes in mood can reliably predict future cognitive decline.

Markova emphasized the importance of studying these relationships over longer periods, particularly as some participants develop more noticeable depression or begin experiencing cognitive difficulties.

It has been revealed that "Future work can continue to track how participants' tau levels and depression symptoms evolve over longer periods of time, particularly as some develop cognitive impairment or more clinically significant levels of depression. Continuing to follow these trajectories, observing how early mood changes relate to later clinical outcomes, and establishing relationships with other methods tracking the development of Alzheimer's disease will provide more clarity on methods to determine which individuals may be at an increased risk.".

Materials provided by Society for Neuroscience. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

The love for South American Heroes continues with Ivan Zamorano presented in his Real Madrid guise rather than part of the unbelievably stacked Inter squad which featured legends and Icons ranging from current Atletico Madrid manager Diego Simeone to Javier Zanetti and Ronaldo Nazario.

Whether her in-game body type will actually let her put that strength out on the pitch (she will surely also have Bruiser) remains to be seen, but she could easily have the gangly aura of Patrick Vieira if the rest of her PlayStyles are right.

New Ultimate Team Heroes have been added mid-season before, including the likes of Enzo Francescoli in FC 24, but 3 at once looks to indicate that EA is leaning on Heroes to add fan-favourite players to the game with a lower threshold than Icons.

Plus they can be given away for free without upsetting the power curve as much as Icons, as shown by the free Classic XI Heroes handed out recently (I got Mario Gomez, F).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s no secret that Grand Theft Auto 6 was not a cheap game to make, to put very, very mildly.
  • Industry observers note that considering the amount of cash that undoubtedly went into GTA 6’s development, which has now been followed by immense success and landmark profits for Rockstar and Take-Two, also in the billions, something of a new precedent has been established for the AAA gaming sector.
  • Obviously, this is completely untrue, but that doesn’t stop people from wondering, especially as far as other power-player devs are concerned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s no secret that Grand Theft Auto 6 was not a cheap game to make, to put very, very mildly. While Rockstar has not publicly disclosed the game’s precise internal price tag, rumors have circulated that it’s somewhere in the billions, and considering the sheer scope and complexity of the game’s world, I don’t think that theory is an unreasonable one.

Industry observers note that considering the amount of cash that undoubtedly went into GTA 6’s development, which has now been followed by immense success and landmark profits for Rockstar and Take-Two, also in the billions, something of a new precedent has been established for the AAA gaming sector. Arguably, it's not a great one: if you keep pouring massive stacks of cash into your game, it’ll magically make billions of dollars forever.

Obviously, this is completely untrue, but that doesn’t stop people from wondering, especially as far as other power-player devs are concerned. For example, CD Projekt Red, developer and publisher of landmark IPs like The Witcher and Cyberpunk, has invested its fair share of capital into its works. However, according to its CEO, Michal Nowakowski, the budget of CDPR’s titles is secondary to their ambitions and goals.

During CD Projekt Red’s Q3 2026 Earnings Call, the audio of which was posted to the firm’s official YouTube channel, Nowakowski was asked his opinion on the “technological and qualitative leap” between Grand Theft Auto 5 and 6, and in turn, how those landmark advancements might inform CDPR’s developmental philosophy going forward, particularly with in-development Witcher and Cyberpunk titles.

Nowakowski acknowledged the major precedent that has been put forth by Rockstar through GTA 6 through the industry at large, but he also clarified that, in spite of that game’s success, he and his tech giant don’t make their games just to compete with those produced by another.

Industry observers note that “If anything happened as a result of GTA 6, it's always great to see games like that because they show you how much cool stuff can be done. That's for sure an inspiration in many ways for our developers.”.

He and his organization don’t make their games just to compete with those produced by another.

When asked how GTA 6’s developmental scope might affect budget expectations for upcoming games, Nowakowski stressed that Witcher and Cyberpunk are not “budget-driven developments,” and while he is always conscious of how much money it costs to make top-shelf games, it’s not really conducive to a product’s health to be constantly keeping the budget in mind during the developmental process.

In a recent development, “They are ambition-driven developments and money is vital, the budgets are not indefinite, that's not what we're saying. And honestly, that philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6.”.

In a recent development, the obvious problem with expecting fresh games, even AAA ones, to have comparable budget and scope to GTA 6 is that not every game is GTA 6, nor is every developer Rockstar. Not everyone is going to have that kind of raw spending power available, and certainly, not everyone has access to the kind of prestige IP with a baked-in fanbase like GTA.

Sources indicate that overbloated budgets for AAA games have already been a consistent problem and talking point for at least a decade now, with players regularly complaining that too much money is spent on making games look visually and technologically impressive without making the core experience any better. This ends up dragging out development cycles and bleeding companies dry, not to mention subjecting developmental staff to intense crunch. Heck, lest we forget, GTA 6 took over a decade itself to come out, and was delayed twice.

Sources indicate that while it is heartening to hear Nowakowski’s proclamation of ambition over budget, it is very difficult to predict where the AAA sector is going now that the shadow of GTA 6 is looming over it. Personally, I’d like to believe that players won’t expect every new game they play to also be GTA 6-tier, but, well….

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1221 w)

Strange fresh materials can crawl, walk, and dig like living creatures

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1221 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that most materials simply react when something pushes, pulls, or bends them.
  • Sources indicate that everyday materials such as metal, concrete, glass, and rubber are generally considered passive.
  • Recent findings suggest that active matter works differently.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that most materials simply react when something pushes, pulls, or bends them. But a very different category of matter can draw on its own energy to change shape and respond to outside forces in surprising ways. Known as active matter, these unusual materials are attracting growing scientific interest. Now, physicists from the universities of Amsterdam, Upcoming South Wales, and Cambridge have uncovered remarkable new behaviors that could change how future machines and robots are designed.

Sources indicate that everyday materials such as metal, concrete, glass, and rubber are generally considered passive. They can stretch, bend, shift, or change shape when forces act on them, but the energy needed to produce those changes comes from outside the material.

Recent findings suggest that active matter works differently. It contains an internal source of energy that allows it to respond to its surroundings in ways ordinary materials cannot. Many examples occur naturally in living systems. A flock of birds, for instance, can move together as a coordinated group, adjusting its behavior in response to wind, changes in the landscape, available food, or a suitable place to rest.

Scientists can also recreate some of these remarkable properties in the laboratory. Researchers from the University of Amsterdam (The Netherlands), the University of Cambridge (UK), and the University of Fresh South Wales (Sydney, Australia) have spent several years developing active materials from surprisingly simple components, including miniature motors, rods, and rubber bands. Their experiments have revealed unusual mechanical behaviors with potentially valuable applications, leading to two recently accepted scientific papers.

Scientists Create Materials That Can Crawl, Walk, and Dig.

One of the discoveries involves two familiar mechanical behaviors known as buckling and snapping.

It has been revealed that imagine squeezing a paper ticket between your fingers. As the pressure increases, the ticket becomes unstable and bends to one side. If you then press against the curved surface, it initially pushes back before suddenly flipping in the opposite direction.

According to recent reports, this is how ordinary passive materials behave. External forces supply the energy needed for the ticket to buckle and snap, and each action occurs only once in response to the applied force.

It has been revealed that the researchers discovered that adding internal activity can fundamentally transform this behavior. They assembled a series of connected rods into a flexible chain, placing small motors at the joints where neighboring rods meet. These motors created interactions that were not symmetrical. Moving one rod could affect its neighbor in a different way than moving that neighbor would affect the original rod (by rotating over a different angle, for example).

Industry observers note that the result was striking. When external forces acted on these active chains, they still bent and snapped, but the movement no longer had to end after a single event. Instead, the structures could repeatedly buckle and snap, producing ongoing oscillations.

The underlying physics involves a transformation of the system's critical point, where snapping normally takes place, into what researchers call a critical exceptional point. This unusual behavior makes it possible for the chains to generate movements resembling crawling, walking, and even digging.

Sources indicate that the findings were published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, with Sami Al-Izzi of the University of New South Wales and Yao Du of the University of Amsterdam serving as joint first authors. One of the team's buckling chains was also featured on the journal's cover.

Industry observers note that beyond revealing unexpected physics, the discovery points toward a promising approach to building materials capable of performing multiple tasks autonomously. Such structures could be especially useful in flexible, "soft" robots, potentially allowing their bodies to produce complex movements without relying on a centralized control system.

Active Matter Challenges a Fundamental Engineering Principle.

A separate investigation by the same international research team uncovered another surprising property of active materials, this time challenging a principle widely used in engineering.

Whether designing large bridges or tiny nanomechanical devices, engineers depend on established rules that connect the properties of individual components to the behavior of an entire structure.

One such rule is Le Chatelier's Principle. In the mechanical context described by the researchers, it suggests that changes made to individual parts of a system should produce corresponding changes in the overall structure. For example, making a structure's individual components stiffer would generally be expected to increase the stiffness of the entire assembly.

Industry observers note that but the researchers found that active matter does not always follow this expectation. In some cases, increasing the activity of individual components can actually reduce the activity of the material as a whole.

Sources indicate that to investigate this counterintuitive effect, the scientists built another structure using motors and rods. Rather than arranging the components in a chain, they connected them into a flat, two-dimensional network resembling a lattice. They then examined how the elastic behavior of the entire structure changed depending on the properties of its individual elements.

Their experiments revealed that the overall response depended on more than simply how active each component was. What mattered was whether the active elements formed connected pathways capable of transmitting mechanical responses throughout the structure.

Why More Activity Can Produce Less Response.

The researchers identified a process called percolation as the key to understanding this unexpected behavior.

A useful comparison is the movement of water through ground coffee. If the coffee grounds are packed too tightly, water cannot easily travel through the entire layer. The arrangement of the grounds determines whether the water can find a continuous path.

Sources indicate that something similar happens inside active materials. If too many of the interconnected components have relatively low activity, they can prevent elastic responses from spreading through the structure. Even when other components are extremely active, their influence may not extend across the entire material.

Industry observers note that this explains why making some parts more active does not necessarily produce a more active structure overall. The way the components are connected and distributed can be just as vital as their individual properties.

The second study, led by first author Jack Binysh from Corentin Coulais's research group at the University of Amsterdam, was published in Physical Review X.

Industry observers note that the researchers believe that this unexpected departure from Le Chatelier's Principle could have notable implications for understanding and designing systems built from active microscopic structures. These include biological gels, epithelial monolayers, which are sheets of closely connected cells, and neuromorphic networks that mimic aspects of biological information processing.

According to recent reports, together, the findings reveal how dramatically materials can behave when their internal components actively consume energy and interact in unconventional ways. The discoveries could influence research across physics, soft matter science, mechanical engineering, the life sciences, and robotics, while opening latest possibilities for creating adaptable materials and smarter robotic systems.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Grand Theft Auto 6 Easter Eggs just keep coming, with the latest involving an NPC who discovered the game’s biggest secret, but vanished before learning the true extent of the conspiracy in their world.

All the Grand Theft Auto games involve massive, sprawling cities, meaning there’s plenty of places for hidden secrets to be stashed. Even Grand Theft Auto 5 still had secrets being uncovered years after launch, with players gradually peeling away the secrets of its UFO sightings.

According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto 6 is no exception when it comes to weird and wonderful secrets, with players finding them within its first week. One of the freakiest discoveries has been chronicled by The Easter Egg Hunter YouTube channel: a mysterious house that has more to it than meets the eye.

It has been revealed that the secret house in Grand Theft Auto 6 actually dates back to Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas Definitive Edition, which added a picture of a mysterious home to one of the bars. Fans discovered that this house exists in Grand Theft Auto 6, in Belville near the mission where Lucia has to deliver vapes.

If the player approaches the house and opens the garage, they’ll find numerous conspiracy theory messages written by the owner, who has discovered the world’s secret: that it’s all just a video game, and he’s an NPC.

Industry observers note that the NPC discovered walk cycles for other people, that killing dogs causes them to respawn, that glitches regularly create freakish people, and that most of the doors in the world don’t work. He also realized that Jason and Lucia were the only people with true freedom, though he couldn’t contact them.

The secret house in Grand Theft Auto 6 actually dates back to Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas Definitive Edition, which added a picture of a mysterious home to one of the bars.

According to recent reports, the NPC also realized that there are no children in the world of Grand Theft Auto 6. This is due to most real-world ratings boards treating violence against kids as a good reason to ban or censor media, which is why most open-world crime games don’t have them.

In a recent development, the fate of the NPC is unknown, but he appears to have tried to escape from the world of Grand Theft Auto 6. He may return in a future enhancement, much like how his house appeared in San Andreas: Definitive Edition, or maybe he’s still in the game and players haven’t found him yet.

The concept of video game characters learning that they’re in a simulacrum of life isn’t a newly introduced one. Characters have been commenting on game mechanics for decades, with many pointing to the original Metal Gear Solid as a prime example, with the barrier between fiction and reality eroding over the course of the series.

It has been revealed that indeed, Grand Theft Auto 6 isn’t even the most prominent example of video game characters learning the truth of their existence and trying to escape. One of the routes in Deltarune Chapter 5 ends with the characters attempting to break out of bounds, though the result won’t be revealed for a few more years.

It’s amazing just how many secrets are packed into Grand Theft Auto 6, with fans already discovering the portal back to the PS2 era and a reference to the Red Hulk from Marvel Comics. One can only wonder what crazy mysteries are still hiding beneath the surface of Vice City, and what else will be added when the game’s inevitable online modes arrive in the future.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yesterday, a rumor emerged on X claiming that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, the upcoming World War II-era superhero game led by Uncharted creator Amy Hennig, was being cancelled. After making the rounds on social media, newly introduced reports claim this is not the case, at least for now.

Recent findings suggest that the rumor stemmed from a now-deleted X post from a fan account called Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown claiming, through supposed inside sources, that Skydance was preparing to announce the game’s cancellation. This rumor was rapidly picked up and circulated by online gaming circles, gaining steam due to growing uncertainty around the game’s status.

It has been revealed that marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was revealed in 2022 and stars Captain America and Black Panther (Azurri, T'Challa's grandfather), alongside Howling Commandos member Gabriel Jones and Wakandan Spy Network leader Nanali, as they battle Hydra during World War II. Developed by Skydance New Media, led by Amy Hennig, it’s been repeatedly delayed, and only cinematic footage has been released. This has understandably caused many to question the game’s fate.

It has been revealed that however, a few hours after the cancellation rumor made the rounds, Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier reported on Bluesky that Skydance’s leadership addressed the rumor with the development team on Slack and assured them Marvel 1943 was not canceled. However, Schreier adds this could change due to the uncertainty caused by the recent merger between Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Skydance (Skydance Latest Media is a game development branch of the now-merged Skydance Corporation).

Skydance Games told the development team behind Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra on Slack this afternoon that the game is not canceled, despite a widely circulated rumor on Twitter today claiming that it was.

Furthermore, Kotaku’s Rebekah Valentine clarified in her report that Marvel 1943 executive producer Lu Giglotti told staff in a Skydance Slack message he’d spoken directly with the executive leadership team to confirm Marvel 1943 is still alive, saying, "There is no truth to these claims." According to Kotaku’s report, Giglotti informed the team that Marvel 1943 was approaching an Alpha milestone later this month. Giglotti also told staff not to let the rumor distract them and that Skydance was "monitoring the situation" to address in the future.

According to recent reports, kotaku’s report also sheds light on the game’s tumultuous development cycle. Marvel 1943 was originally pitched as a Netflix game before it was eventually turned into a console and PC title. This transition means the current iteration is “light on gameplay” and lacks substantial interactions, with players primarily using a single button to play it.

This isn't a completely surprising revelation, as Marvel 1943 was billed as a narrative-driven, linear single-player experience when it was revealed, but the style of game has never been clear. The same reveal also saw Skydance promise the game boasted "intuitive controls and exhilarating second-to-second gameplay that captures the action and excitement of Marvel, inspired by landmark comics, television, and films, as they navigate this all-latest globe-trotting adventure." This disconnect may be attributed to Kotaku also reporting that Marvel 1943 is “well over budget,” and its overall scope has been heavily scaled back. Regardless, the outlet’s source claims the game is “close to done.”.

According to recent reports, marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was initially slated to launch in 2025. It was then delayed to early 2026 "to add more polish", according to Skydance, before being pushed again to an undetermined launch window. The game has no announced platforms.

Industry observers note that although Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra appears safe for now, other recent projects have not been as fortunate. Be sure to read our stories about the recent high-profile cancellations of Gang of Dragon and Fairgames.

[Sources: Jason Schreier, Kotaku].

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that vince Zampella, known for co-creating the Call of Duty series, among many other roles, has died. Zampella, 55, died in a car crash in Los Angeles on Sunday. The fatal crash killed him, along with the occupant of his car.

Recent findings suggest that according to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles. Zampella was unfortunately trapped in an ensuing car fire, and the passenger was ejected.

Industry observers note that vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators. His storied career is long, and is responsible for some of the biggest shooter franchises in history. It started with Medal of Honor in the 90s, a game that changed WW2 shooters forever.

It has been revealed that zampella later co-founded the legendary Infinity Ward in 2002, the team that would go on to redefine multiplayer shooters forever. Infinity Ward is the studio responsible for the Call of Duty series, which remains one of the biggest games for publisher Activision, and the entire industry.

Recent findings suggest that zampella then left the studio he founded in 2010 following a major fallout with Activision. He, along with longtime collaborator, Jason West, went to rival publisher EA to form Respawn Entertainment.

Respawn went on to create the Titanfall series, and later Apex Legends. The studio is responsible for non-shooters, of course, like the third-person action game series Star Wars Jedi. Zampella was instrumental in making the game possible, having hired God of War 3 director Stig Asmussen to helm a team within Respawn out of a desire to diversify the studio’s output and prove he can do more than make shooters.

According to recent reports, zampella had only recently met with journalists and peers at The Game Awards, where Battlefield 6 was nominated for multiple awards. Battlefield 6 is the most successful game in series history, in part as a result of Zampella’s leadership. The legendary leader was given the reigns of the struggling multiplayer shooter franchise in 2021, with a goal of finding a viable future.

Zampella’s sudden death has shaken the industry, and many mourn his loss as the news started spreading.

“We are heartbroken by the loss of Vince Zampella, a creative leader whose work shaped generations of players and helped define what modern shooters and action games could be,” EA stated in a statement.

“While his impact reached far beyond any one game or studio, we will remember Vince for how he indicated up every day, trusting his teams, encouraging bold ideas, and believing in Battlefield and the people building it. We are deeply grateful for his leadership, his generosity, and the care he brought to everything he touched, and we will carry that forward with us.”.

U.S. loses measles elimination status after 25 years as vaccine myths persist

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1302 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The United States has lost its measles elimination status after more than 25 years, marking a major setback in the fight against a highly contagious disease.
  • In a recent development, the United States first achieved measles elimination status in 2000.
  • Recent findings suggest that the announcement comes during the country's worst measles resurgence in decades.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The United States has lost its measles elimination status after more than 25 years, marking a major setback in the fight against a highly contagious disease. At the same time, a newly introduced nationwide survey from the Annenberg Public Policy Center (APPC) reveals that many Americans remain confused about the dangers of measles and the vaccines that protect against it.

In a recent development, the United States first achieved measles elimination status in 2000. This designation meant that no strain of the virus had spread continuously within the country for 12 months or longer. However, on Nov. 17, 2026, the Pan American Health Organization confirmed that the United States no longer qualified for that status.

Recent findings suggest that the announcement comes during the country's worst measles resurgence in decades. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the United States had recorded 5,412 confirmed cases in 2026 as of Nov. 12. That is more than twice the 2,290 cases reported throughout all of 2025.

Vaccine Myths Persist Despite Decades of Scientific Evidence.

A November 2026 Annenberg Science and Public Health (ASAPH) survey, conducted using adults from the SSRS Omnibus survey, highlights widespread misunderstandings about childhood vaccination. Nearly two-thirds of Americans (64%) correctly rejected the claim that "vaccines given to children for diseases like measles, mumps, and rubella cause autism." However, 17% believed the claim was true, while another 19% said they did not know whether it was true or false.

Industry observers note that the results closely resemble findings from earlier APPC research. Across four surveys involving a separate sample of U.S. adults (September 2024 to August 2026), the ongoing ASAPH national probability survey found that 65% to 68% correctly rejected a connection between childhood vaccines and autism (65%-68%). Another 12% to 14% incorrectly believed there was a connection (12%-14%), while 19% to 22% remained uncertain.

The latest survey also asked respondents to compare autism rates among fully vaccinated and unvaccinated children. Nearly half (49%) believed both groups were "about as likely" to show signs of autism. Another 11% thought fully vaccinated children were "more likely" to show signs, 14% believed they were "less likely," and 26% could not say.

According to recent reports, extensive scientific research has found no evidence that vaccines cause autism. In 2004, the National Academy of Medicine (then named the Institute of Medicine) concluded that "the body of epidemiological evidence favors rejection of a causal relationship between the MMR vaccine and autism evidence.".

Industry observers note that the World Health Organization's Global Advisory Committee on Vaccine Safety reached the same conclusion in 2025, reaffirming that high-quality scientific evidence does not establish a causal relationship between vaccination and autism. FactCheck.org, which is operated by the Annenberg Public Policy Center, has also challenged claims linking vaccines to autism, explaining that the evidence does not support them.

These misconceptions may have consequences for vaccination decisions. Previous Annenberg research found that people who accept false vaccine claims, including the belief that the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine causes autism, are less likely to recommend MMR vaccination to people who are eligible to receive it.

Only 9% of Americans Know How Deadly Measles Can Be.

The survey uncovered another striking knowledge gap. Most Americans appear uncertain about the risk of death associated with measles in children.

Recent findings suggest that when asked how many children infected with measles are likely to die from the disease, 59% of respondents noted they did not know. Just 9% selected the correct response, "about 1 in 1,000," which most closely matches the CDC’s estimate that 1 to 3 of every 1,000 infected children die from respiratory or neurological complications.

Nearly one-quarter of respondents (23%) underestimated the death rate, while another 9% selected a higher rate.

Recent findings suggest that knowledge about measles vaccination was also limited. Almost half of Americans (49%) stated they were unsure how many doses children need for full protection. Only about one-third (34%) correctly identified the recommended two-dose schedule.

According to recent reports, the CDC advises giving children their first MMR vaccine dose between 12 and 15 months of age, followed by a second dose between ages 4 and 6. According to CDC data, a single dose provides 93% protection against measles, while receiving both doses increases effectiveness to 97%.

According to recent reports, public Confidence in Robert F. Kennedy Jr. Remains Low.

According to recent reports, the survey also examined Americans' trust in U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. The findings indicate that public confidence in his health-related communications has changed little since earlier surveys conducted in 2025 and 2026.

Industry observers note that in November 2026, about six in 10 respondents (61%) said they were not confident that Kennedy was providing trustworthy information about public health. The remaining four in 10 (39%) expressed confidence in the information he provides.

These results are consistent with seven earlier national probability surveys conducted over two years (February 2025 to August 2026). During that period, 60% to 63% of respondents reported lacking confidence in Kennedy, while 37% to 39% expressed confidence.

Kathleen Hall Jamieson, director of the Annenberg Public Policy Center's Science of Science Communication Institute and its ASAPH and ASK surveys, said the loss of measles elimination status demonstrates the consequences of declining vaccination coverage.

"The announcement that the U.S. has lost its measles elimination status confirms what we already knew," said Kathleen Hall Jamieson. "Those who refused the MMR vaccine for themselves or their children and those who misled them into doing so have produced the tragic effects that science predicted would occur when community immunity dropped below the threshold needed to protect those who are not able to be vaccinated or refused to be.".

How the National Measles Survey Was Conducted.

The findings draw on two types of Annenberg Science and Public Health (ASAPH) surveys.

The November 2026 results come from a nationally representative survey of 1,028 U.S. adults conducted for APPC by SSRS, an independent market research organization. Participants were selected from the manufacturer's probability-based online opinion panel, and responses were collected Nov. 6-8, 2026. The survey has a margin of sampling error (MOE) of ± 3.5 percentage points at the 95% confidence level.

The other findings come from APPC's ongoing ASAPH panel surveys, which are also administered by SSRS. Participants were originally recruited through probability sampling from the SSRS Opinion Panel, and their responses are weighted to reflect the U.S. adult population. This research panel operates separately from the SSRS Omnibus survey and has completed more than 30 survey waves since April 2021.

Percentages are rounded to the nearest whole number, so totals may not always equal 100%.

Additional results are available in the survey topline, which includes data from both the November 2026 omnibus survey and the ongoing ASAPH panel surveys. A separate methodology statement provides further details about the latest survey.

Since April 2021, the Annenberg Public Policy Center has used its Annenberg Science and Public Health (ASAPH) research program and separate national samples to monitor Americans' knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors related to vaccines, Covid-19, influenza, RSV, and other notable health issues.

The APPC health survey team includes Ken Winneg, managing director of survey research; Laura A. Gibson, research analyst; and Patrick E. Jamieson, director of the Annenberg Health and Risk Communication Institute.

In a recent development, materials provided by Annenberg Public Policy Center of the University of Pennsylvania. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that genshin Impact’s latest Special Program has spilled all the beans on the game’s next major patch, Luna 4. The update, which arrives on January 14, kicks off 2026 with several bits of latest content, including some previously-teased characters.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three newly introduced playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

In a recent development, the first latest arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

In a recent development, the Moon Maiden’s special ability, Lunar Domain, further boosts all Lunar Reactions by applying a DMG bonus, including summoning more thundercloud strikes for Lunar-Charged reactions. Columbina is also capable of converting Electro-Charged, Bloom, and Hydro Crystallize reactions into Lunar Reactions, as well as revive fallen squad members.

Speaking of elemental reactions, newly introduced in this version is Lunar-Crystallize, a new reaction that’s triggered when Geo meets Hydro (under certain conditions). When triggered, Lunar-Crystallize summons three Moondrifts near enemies. When triggered three times, Moondrift Harmony gets activated, dealing Geo DMG to enemies caught in its radius.

According to recent reports, then there’s Zibai, an Adeptus from Liyue. Zibai is another 5-Star character, a Geo Sword wielder. Zibai can, through entering a special state where they can build up energy, unleash an Elemental Skill that deals Lunar-Crystallize DMG.

The longer the fight goes on, the more Lunar-Crystallize reactions are triggered, the higher (and more often) the damage of Zibai’s Elemental Skill becomes.

Luna 4 continues the Nod-Krai story arc, with a major confrontation with Il Dottore. This is the focus of the newly introduced Archon Quest, completing which will earn you a new outfit. There’s a gameplay element to that new chapter, too, with the reveal of Piramida, a new area north of the region. Piramida is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers.

According to recent reports, the first phase of Luna 4’s Event Wishes will, unsurprisingly, feature Columbina. It’ll also include reruns of Ineffa. The second phase is when Zibai becomes available, alongside another newcomer: Illuga, a 4-Star, polearm-wielding Geo Lightkeeper. The second phase’s rerun will be Neuvillette, who’s also going to have a new outfit in the shop at a discount.

Version Luna 4 brings back the annual Lantern Rite event, taking place in the mainland of Liyue. The event features its own set of minigames with unique rewards, alongside new stories of the Adepti.

It has been revealed that all around Liyue Harbor, you’ll be able to place Xiao Lanterns and inscribe them with messages for others to read. You’ll also earn some Fortune Coins from Auspicious Treasure Trees, which you can later exchange for gifts.

Finally, you can look forward to the new Classic Mode in Miliastra Wonderland, which lets you invite select Teyvat characters to join you.

Showa American Story Has Been Delayed

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you were feeling like today was a good day for killing some zombies in a Japanese-American setting as a teenage girl brought back from the dead, this might not be a happy day for you, as Showa American Story has been pushed back for a later release.
  • According to recent reports, the game was originally revealed by NEKCOM back in January 2022, known as Project SAS.
  • The announcement was made through NEKCOM’s social media, where they confirmed the official launch for October 28, 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you were feeling like today was a good day for killing some zombies in a Japanese-American setting as a teenage girl brought back from the dead, this might not be a happy day for you, as Showa American Story has been pushed back for a later release.

According to recent reports, the game was originally revealed by NEKCOM back in January 2022, known as Project SAS. While it had no initial release date, the game was later unveiled (now with its proper name) for the PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, and Steam. As production went on, the team had to let go of the former version, and after some more delays, it’s now projected to come out officially in 2027.

The announcement was made through NEKCOM’s social media, where they confirmed the official launch for October 28, 2027. The announcement reaffirms the team’s focus on “polishing and optimizing the experience” for the title before its official release. This has been a frequent move by developers over the last few years, and probably for the best.

Industry observers note that notable titles that went through the same way include Assassin’s Creed Shadows, Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, and, of course, GTA 6, which all took some extra time to guarantee a perfectly-tuned experience for the players. And with so many Easter eggs and secrets to discover in some of those games, it’s hard to say this was a bad call.

In a recent development, showa American Story had its release date first revealed back in 2024, projected for a 2025 window. However, the game was pushed back to 2026 to ensure its development would go smoothly. And while it’s now being pushed back once again, we can probably rest assured that this should be the last time, as it now has a fixed date for its release.

The announcement reaffirms the team’s focus on ‘polishing and optimizing the experience’ for the title before its official release.

The Chinese RPG game was first conceptualized back in 2016, but only entered official development during this decade. It follows an alternative timeline where the United States has been heavily influenced by Japan, bringing a chaotic amalgamation of cultures to life. Oh, and we have zombies too.

We follow the story of Chigusa Choko, a 19-year-old stuntwoman who has been brought back to life alongside hordes of undead. After awakening years after her death, in the so-called Showa era 66, Choko is looking for answers to why she is back in this period, and what has transpired to make the world fall into such disorder. It’s just your average zombie movie, but with some interesting quirks.

A good example is how Choko has some kind of unique power. Her physical capacities are greatly enhanced, and she can easily make her way through the waves of mindlessly acting bodies. But with a lot of gore, of course. From melee weapons to heavy gunfire, she has tons of ways to make quick work of her fellow undead.

Sources indicate that but the main attraction here is the amazing “Showa America” culture, combining both of the best and the worst aspects of the Showa Era in Japan and our ever-loving American Dream in one. The 80s and 90s culture of both countries is presented as one, so it’s not uncommon to catch one of the other survivors in this apocalyptic setting to gush over their favorite anime right after saluting their flag.

With your usual amount of special moves coming straight out of a B-movie, plenty of dark humor, and a lot of love for both the represented cultures, Showa American Story is definitely a title I’m excited to hear more about. And as the industry grows ever so demanding, I’m glad to see it’ll have some extra time to cook. It's done wonders for GTA, so I can’t complain about it now.

Vampire Therapist review - “The problems of unlife aren't so black and white.”

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1248 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pocketgamer
