    GTA 6: Where to Find Cave Diving

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (497 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dualshockers

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • ​There feels like endless activities to do in Grand Theft Auto 6.
    • According to recent reports, most of the side activities are hidden, not properly introduced or shown on the map where to find them, and that’s exactly the case for cave diving.
    • Industry observers note that the cave system isn’t too far off from where you start in chapter 2 of the story.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    ​There feels like endless activities to do in Grand Theft Auto 6. Whether it’s racing through the streets of Vice City, playing mini-golf with your loved one or robbing banks, there’s no shortage of things to do in this vast open world adventure.

    According to recent reports, most of the side activities are hidden, not properly introduced or shown on the map where to find them, and that’s exactly the case for cave diving. This dangerous and claustrophobic activity might not be for everyone, but it certainly can yield you some good rewards if you decide to bring Jason or Lucia down.

    Industry observers note that the cave system isn’t too far off from where you start in chapter 2 of the story. You will be able to access it in the first chapter, but it will be a bit of a drive. This is located all the way in Kelly County. This can be found in the western portion of the map.

    The best way to find where you’re going is right in-between the L and E on the Leonida text if you zoom all the way out on the map. You will see a rather large network of swamps and rivers called the Emerald Springs. Here, you will want to go directly west of the “Emerald Springs” text on the map, around the rivers and on the western side.

    There will be a small hut area on the map that branches off from the road, and this will lead to Selkie Hole. The Selkie is a mythological creature from Norse and Celtic lore. Up here, you will spot various divers and a couple of them just leave their scuba gear out there. Grab them (they won’t care) and head inside the cave through the chain-link door. Down the stairs is the cave system. Happy exploring!

    A light illuminates rocks in a dark underwater cave, with an Explorer’s Knife prompt on screen.

    Sadly, most of the cave system is already mapped – literally. You’ll be able to open up your in-game map and see just how far the tunnels go, and that’s all there is. Now, we say “that’s all there is”, but in reality, it’s a surprisingly lengthy and sprawling system that will take quite a bit to fully explore.

    Industry observers note that because of that, there will be some hidden items spread throughout. One of the most common items in this cave system is Meteorites. These are unique items spread throughout the open world in which you’ll be able to pawn for some extra cash, usually for quite a bit (especially early on). It’s the same as collectibles such as cards and doubloons, but yielding the most trade value.

    On top of that, you will find other unique items such as an Explorer’s Knife pretty close to the entrance of the cave system. It’s nothing too special but one that you will always have considering it’s a legendary weapon.

    #120889. While soulslikes went bigger than massive, Death's Door swung open the appeal of a tighter adventure

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (556 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

    While soulslikes went bigger than massive, Death's Door swung open the appeal of a tighter adventure

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (556 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the big, bulging ones.
    • Even in the latter stages, with a full kit of precisely four ranged spells, Death’s Door is a simple proposition.
    • In a recent development, still, it’s clever with its limitations.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the big, bulging ones. Elden Rings and Silksongs, with vast kingdoms and deep, rattling toolkits for surviving them. The reason it’s a fool’s game is because you can also have something like Death’s Door, a taut, compact, lighthearted little actioner that fills eight hours instead of 80 and yet never feels underwhelming or compromised for it.

    Even in the latter stages, with a full kit of precisely four ranged spells, Death’s Door is a simple proposition. You are a crow. You hit things. Occasionally you shoot things. You collect the souls of a frog, a yeti, and a grandmother. Everything in-between directly relates to finding the errant monster/pensioner, or at a stretch, upgrading one of those four abilities.

    In a recent development, still, it’s clever with its limitations. Environments are small in number but vary wildly in tone and texture, and they tightly weave their paths into criss-crossing bundles that maximise travel – evoking the sense of a great, ranging adventure within relatively tiny spaces. The lack of a wiki’s worth of combat options also never becomes a problem, partly because it spreads out its spell unlocks, and partly because the smooth, flowing back-and-forths of its central swordplay are pleasurable enough to carry it anyway. Good bosses, too! They’re all characterful, memorable weirdoes who fight unlike anyone in their minion armies, and usually come with a hidden weakness to deduce and exploit.

    Which is welcome, as these significant lads and lasses do tend to launch difficulty spikes right up your feathered backside, and do so in a game that isn’t otherwise as fussed about trial-and-error pain endurance as some of its inspirations. They don’t, however, bring the mood down. At times, this tale of a pitch-black soul reaper working as an agent of Death (complete with an office of Death and embittered co-workers of Death) can get downright cosy, leading through you through warmly-lit jungles and breezy waterside ruins.

    Recently replaying, I’d also forgotten how witty it can be. Little gaglets are sprinkled throughout, both visual and verbal, but the best jokes are saved for – funnily enough – the bosses, who’ll raise your pre-fight spirit with some amusingly terrible trash talk before becoming the punchline themselves. I audibly wheezed the first time a death animation immediately cut to the foe’s impromptu funeral, their beaked killer among the precious few guests. And even when the joke is recycled later, I couldn’t help tittering at the sight of my enemy – who seconds earlier, had been attempting to fatally sit on me – lying nobly in state.

    According to recent reports, I previously considered ending my Valor Mortis review by calling it a gateway into the more demanding side of action-RPGs; a shorter, simpler alternative to FromSoft’s overwhelming titans that might nonetheless serve to introduce curious newcomers to their shared quirks and qualities. The game equivalent of splashing your chest with water before jumping into a pool. In hindsight, Death’s Door was always a better fit for that description, though there’s enough else here you don’t need to be prepping for something tougher to appreciate its lean, keen adventuring.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love.
    • As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year.
    • The standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love. Today, we learned the list of nominees for the 2027 Grammy ceremony, and it's an interesting lineup. The nominations are as follows:.

    As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year. On that note, it's most surprising to see that Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora has been nominated for the third year in a row: once for the base game, once for the Secrets of the Spires DLC, and now for the From The Ashes DLC. None of these soundtracks are bad by any means, but their Grammy representation far outweighs their cultural footprint.

    The standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into. However, it's also a Sony-published game, which have a pretty good track record of getting nominations, potentially due to the company's massive presence in the music and film industries. Still, Ghost of Yōtei has a great, unique score that's deserving of its spot, and also one previously nominated for best music at the 2025 Game Awards. The Grammys accept any releases between October 1 of one year and September 30 of the following year, so Ghost of Yōtei barely made the cut for this window. The Game Awards nominees will be announced tomorrow – it will be interesting to see how much overlap there is between the categories.

    This batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years. This is Gordy Haab's third nomination (he won in 2024 for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor) and John Paesano's second nomination (he was nominated in 2025 for Marvel's Spider-Man 2). It's also the first year since the awards' creation without Bear McCreary or Austin Wintory nominations.

    According to recent reports, last year's nominations left a sour taste in the mouths of many, with several DLC nominees and a complete lack of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the year's standout hit that many specifically praised for its music. This year certainly has snubs (Mewgenics, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Control Resonant all come to mind), but none as egregious as last year.

    What do you think was the best video game score from the last year? Let us know in the comments!

    Industry News: After 15 years, The Sims' best spin-off finally gets its due follow-up in The Sims 4: Royalty & Legacy

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that the Sims 4 developers recently promised an exciting year for the game, and the franchise as a whole, and we just got an early look at one of those first events.
    • Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.
    • According to recent reports, there’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that the Sims 4 developers recently promised an exciting year for the game, and the franchise as a whole, and we just got an early look at one of those first events. After some light teasing, the developer unveiled Royalty & Legacy, the game’s next expansion.

    Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.

    According to recent reports, there’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40. For one, it introduces a latest world, Ondarion, which is going to be the setting for your kingdom, as you join a race for the throne. The expansion introduces Dynasty and Nobility - two new systems you can use to create your own world of royal shenanigans.

    Ondarion is made up of three neighborhoods (regions). Each region has a unique theme and culture, and they’re each ruled by a Dynasty. Dambele is a place that prioritises art and community. Verdemar is a chaotic world of outlaws and nobles. Finally, Bellacorde is an extravagant region known for opulence and romance.

    It has been revealed that speaking of building places, Royalty & Legacy also adds a latest Lot type, The Backroom Lot. It serves two functions that change with the time of day. For instance, it can be a library or gym in the morning, and shift into a night club at night. Dambele has its own library-turned-rave, for instance.

    Industry observers note that at the heart of Ondarion are all the possible fantasy lives and stories you can live. The Sims calls them Powershifts, and they include some well-known Arthurian fantasies and other, more silly ones.

    Swordsmanship is the new 10-level skill arriving with the expansion, which further plays into those fantasies by letting your Sims duel. There are even Swordsmanship Tournaments you can watch take place across every neighborhood in Ondarion.

    According to recent reports, then there are Secret Passageways, which let you speed up moving across the new regions. They essentially let your Sims teleport between designated passageways, either on their own lots, or other lots in the world. Some of these are hidden for you to find, while others you can create.

    In terms of upcoming careers, there’s the Noble Career, where your Sim can rise through several Noble Rankings by doing basically what nobles had to do in the middle ages to earn favour.

    The aforementioned Dynasty System is how you can join any of Ondarion’s existing families, or start your own. You actually have a lot of say in what goes on, including the usual business of appointing heirs.

    Recent findings suggest that of course, no royal roleplay would be complete without scandals, which is where the Scandals System comes in. Through it, you can create stories to discredit others, or even topple an entire dynasty.

    In November, you may recall The Sims 4 introducing newly introduced free items inspired by West African culture. In creating that content, EA worked with a group of Simmers who have direct ties to West African countries.

    The group’s guidance was once again utilised to build the Dambele neighborhood in this expansion, and some of the lots around the world of Ondarion were even created by members of the group.

    While you wait for Royalty & Legacy to actually arrive, there’s more in The Sims 4 you can jump in right now. The game recently kicked off a collaboration with fashion brand Coach that brought several free items to Create a Sim, and Build Buy. That arrived alongside a free patch, which already makes for a busy start of the year for The Sims 4.

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Live service games have it rough in the current gaming industry, forced to fight tooth and nail against half a dozen well-established titles that have all but consumed the worthwhile player base.
    • It has been revealed that some, like Capcom’s Exoprimal, try to throw everything at the wall to see what sticks with players, and I can’t lie, mech suits vs dinosaurs was a compelling first pitch.
    • Marked for death after September 2027, players have less than a year to enjoy their Jurassic jungle gym.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Live service games have it rough in the current gaming industry, forced to fight tooth and nail against half a dozen well-established titles that have all but consumed the worthwhile player base. Anyone new on the block needs to really justify their airtime, and for many, it’s simply not worth the hassle of getting torn apart by consumers.

    It has been revealed that some, like Capcom’s Exoprimal, try to throw everything at the wall to see what sticks with players, and I can’t lie, mech suits vs dinosaurs was a compelling first pitch. After three solid years of support, however, Exoprimal is facing End of Service, just announced by Capcom.

    Marked for death after September 2027, players have less than a year to enjoy their Jurassic jungle gym.

    According to recent reports, exoprimal was an odd title, announced back in 2022 and released in July of 2023. One of Capcom's few big-budget standalone titles, surrounded by its long-running franchises, Exoprimal was Capcom’s attempt to leap into the third-person shooter live-service genre dominated by Warframe.

    Exoprimal itself found a niche audience that enjoyed what was on offer, with a humble but positive review on Steam to this day. Despite the receptive crowd, players were disappointed by the lack of content on launch, leaving them with plenty of hunger for more dino-killing, mech-fueled action.

    Sources indicate that capcom eventually relented in a series of effective but spaced-out patches, leaving players feeling like the second fiddle as the company continued to focus on its heavy hitters. The End of Service announcement is a genuine death sentence for a title like Exoprimal, not just revealing an end to active development, but a date the game will be simply unplayable after.

    Recent findings suggest that the announcement is unfortunate, but sadly not at all unexpected. When compared to other middling live service ventures, Exoprimal managing a total of 4 years of support is on the higher end. This, sadly, just means players who put in the time are left in the dust, at least until they find a third-party way to keep playing.

    Anyone upcoming on the block needs to really justify their airtime, and for many, it’s simply not worth the hassle of getting torn apart by consumers.

    Modders have been the absolute team players when it comes to keeping the lights on for live service communities, and Exoprimal is no different. If they can’t, Exoprimal is facing downright elimination, a sad sight for one of Capcom’s most video-gamey new titles that could absolutely have made it in the long haul.

    End-of-Service announcements have killed tons of games, both strong and weak. It’s been a major hit to the industry, with half of the recent releases that drop threatened by an eventual death knell. Any investment in a title that isn’t guaranteed to succeed, like massive franchise sequels, feels like a gamble, and it can be absolutely exhausting.

    Sources indicate that capcom is one company that can absolutely afford to put out smaller, standalone titles to make some cash and potentially introduce whole newly introduced franchises. Pragmata is one such gem, a fantastic little puzzle shooter that came out of nowhere. A perfect little bite-sized adventure is perfectly Capcom, and their care for anything other than Monster Hunter indicates they just truly aren’t great with long-term support.

    Compared to Monster Hunter, with its constant newly introduced hunts, events, and short-term content to keep players engaged over time, all the while hyping a massive expansion just over the horizon. Exoprimal struggled to offer anything beyond cosmetics and microtransactions for short-term content between missions, making it clear the small team working on the title didn’t get much focus.

    Industry observers note that sadly, Exoprimal’s cancellation isn't surprising, but the fanbase isn’t going anywhere. They may be small, but they’ve got the passion and effort to try and keep the party going, at least for a while longer.

The results crown a strong Counter-Strike year eight days before the next CS2 Major begins in Singapore.

    The 2026 Esports Awards honoured two British figures from the streaming and broadcast side of the scene. Caedrel is a League of Legends streamer and co-streamer. Gaskin works as a caster.

    The ceremony took place on the evening of 17 November at the Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts of Miami-Dade County. It is the scene’s main end-of-season awards show. The event began in London in 2016.

    At Worlds 2026, Caedrel was the top co-streamer for both hours watched and peak viewers, according to Esports Charts.

    In a recent development, his co-stream success came in a softer year for the tournament overall. Worlds 2026 peaked at 3.98 million viewers, which was 41% lower than the previous year. Caedrel’s numbers show how much attention a single co-streamer can hold even when the event’s headline peak falls.

    In a recent development, gaskin was not the only caster honoured in Miami. The other broadcast honours went to Alex ‘Machine’ Richardson for Play-by-Play Caster of the Year, Iain Chambers for Host of the Year and Anthony ‘NAMELESS’ Wheeler for Analyst of the Year. iShowSpeed was named Streamer of the Year.

    Counter-Strike featured prominently among the industry prizes. Vitality’s award as best organisation came alongside Esports PC Player of the Year for Mathieu ‘ZywOo’ Herbaut. OpTic Texas were named Esports Team of the Year.

    BLAST, which stages many of its events in Europe, was named Esports Tournament Organiser of the Year.

    Sources indicate that vitality’s results through the year back up their award. They beat Spirit to win IEM Rio 2026 on 19 April, giving them back-to-back ESL Grand Slam titles. ZywOo took his 31st career HLTV MVP award at that event.

    "When I won this award in 2023, I never thanked my parents" 😅❤️.

    Esports Colour Caster of the Year — @DanGaskin pic.twitter.com/oZBw5FItEJ.

    — Esports Awards Presented by Thunderpick (@esportsawards) November 18, 2026.

    The team’s form held into the autumn. Vitality swept MOUZ 3-0 in the ESL Pro League Season 24 grand final on 11 October. That was their second title in a row after winning StarSeries Fall in September.

    The PGL Major Singapore 2026 runs from 25 November to 13 December with 32 teams and a US$1,250,000 prize pool, The Kallang reported. The final stages will be played at the Singapore Indoor Stadium from 10 to 13 December.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that mucky and disreputable kiosk game Probably Stolen – Cyberpunk Shopkeeper Sim is getting three big updates over the next few months that add extra starting scenarios, building on the existing wealth of goods, materials, vocations and techs. Those starting scenarios range from peddling human meat to running the finest cyber-frappucino stall this side of Tannhäuser Gate. There are no hard release dates, and the contents of each revision may alter, but developers Questing Goose Studio have shared some rough timeframes.

    Coming up in mid-December, there's the Junker starting scenario, which I assume is all about trading scrap, rather than being a Prussian nobleman. You'll get a bespoke perk, new items, and the ability to hire, equip and send scavs on expeditions. This upgrade will also include some minor expansions for the Fence and Gunsmith vocations – the latter will be able to flog or otherwise make use of shotgun shells, 25mm grenade rounds and a tier 3 handmade SMG, alongside new armour.

    It has been revealed that late January is when you'll "very likely" get the chance to be an Organ Dealer, care of the second major update. "Players will start by buying different organs and fulfilling specific requests, and will later be able to grow or print organs," a Steam blog explains. You'll also be able to filter blood and remove diseases, with different blood types having different value modifiers. How will you get your hands on organs? By sending horrible black market thugs on foraging "expeditions".

    Last but not least, the planned April enhancement will add the Street Food Vendor starting scenario. This lets you weave a livelihood around choice beverages and edibles from a range of cultures, supported by updates to the game's Aquaculture and Hydroponics tech. Sounds a lot cheerier than the organ trading racket, but then again, Probably Stolen will doubtless find a way to make it utterly grim. Guests at Sweeney's Cantina know better than to ask what our frappucinos are made of.

    It has been revealed that are you playing Probably Stolen? It's been doing better than expected. I was keen on the demo, but my attention was lured away by a truly upsetting game about dogpeople in caves.

    #120882. Breaking: Scientists discover a hidden gut defense that could prevent colon cancer

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1842 w)

    Breaking: Scientists discover a hidden gut defense that could prevent colon cancer

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1842 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that A common antibody found throughout the digestive tract may provide an unexpected defense against colon cancer.
    • In a recent development, in a study published in Nature, scientists found that mice missing a type of antibody known as immunoglobulin A (IgA) developed more than twice as many colon tumors as mice with normal levels of the antibody.
    • Even more promising, when the team administered IgA orally to mice that lacked the antibody, the animals no longer showed an elevated risk of developing tumors.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that A common antibody found throughout the digestive tract may provide an unexpected defense against colon cancer. Researchers at Rockefeller University have discovered that these immune molecules help regulate the growth of cells lining the intestine, potentially preventing the uncontrolled cell division that can lead to tumors.

    In a recent development, in a study published in Nature, scientists found that mice missing a type of antibody known as immunoglobulin A (IgA) developed more than twice as many colon tumors as mice with normal levels of the antibody. The researchers also uncovered how this protection works. IgA attaches to cells along the intestinal lining and helps prevent them from multiplying too rapidly.

    Even more promising, when the team administered IgA orally to mice that lacked the antibody, the animals no longer showed an elevated risk of developing tumors.

    According to recent reports, "One intriguing aspect of this work is that it reveals how a natural defense in the gut restrains the cell division that can lead to cancer," indicates senior author Daniel Mucida, who leads Rockefeller's Laboratory of Mucosal Immunology. "Most cancer research focuses on trying to destroy a tumor that already exists, but what if we could intervene before tumors form?".

    Sources indicate that the findings may help explain why people with IgA deficiency, a condition in which the body produces little or none of this antibody, face a greater risk of colorectal cancer. They also offer latest insight into how gut bacteria, immune defenses, and intestinal cells work together to influence cancer development, potentially even in people with otherwise healthy immune systems.

    Why the Gut Contains So Much of This Antibody.

    Sources indicate that igA is one of the immune system's most abundant antibodies in the digestive tract, where it provides an key early defense against potentially harmful microbes. Unlike antibodies that recognize a single specific target, IgA can interact with many different kinds of gut bacteria and even certain healthy cells belonging to the body.

    Sources indicate that scientists have known for decades that the intestines contain unusually large quantities of IgA. However, the reasons for its abundance, and the full range of functions it performs, have remained incompletely understood.

    Mucida's laboratory investigates how the intestine manages two essential but sometimes competing responsibilities. It must defend the body against dangerous microorganisms while allowing nutrients from food to pass into the bloodstream. Earlier research from his team has also helped explain how immune cells in the digestive tract contribute to food intolerances and allergies.

    For the new study, Gregory Donaldson, a former postdoctoral researcher at Rockefeller who is now an assistant professor at UCLA, set out to better understand how IgA interacts with intestinal bacteria and whether those interactions might influence the development of colon cancer.

    "We know these antibodies bind bacteria and, by doing so, can shape the microbiome," he claims. "And because IgA deficiency, which affects about 1 in 500 people in the U.S., is linked to colorectal cancer, I wondered whether these interactions might be relevant to the disease.".

    The microbiome is the community of microorganisms living in and on the body. In the intestines, these microbes perform important functions related to digestion and immune health, but certain bacteria can also contribute to disease under the wrong conditions.

    Missing Gut Antibodies More Than Doubled Colon Tumors.

    It has been revealed that to investigate IgA's protective effects, Donaldson compared mice that could not produce the antibody with mice that had normal IgA levels. Both groups were raised together, allowing the researchers to control for differences in food and exposure to microorganisms.

    The results revealed a striking difference. Animals without IgA developed substantially more colorectal tumors than their counterparts, consistent with the increased colorectal cancer risk observed in humans with IgA deficiency.

    Sources indicate that the association was not limited to a single experimental setup. Researchers observed the same pattern using multiple models of colon cancer, strengthening the evidence that IgA plays a meaningful protective role.

    "We found this was true for several different kinds of models of colon cancer, so that was a really convincing effect," says Donaldson.

    In a recent development, the team then tested whether replacing the missing antibody could reverse the effect. When mice lacking IgA received oral doses of the antibody, their increased susceptibility to colon tumors disappeared.

    This result suggested that IgA does more than simply accompany other protective processes in the intestine. Its presence appears to directly influence conditions that determine whether tumors develop.

    Scientists Discover a Natural Brake on Cancer Cell Growth.

    To understand the mechanism behind this protection, the researchers examined epithelial cells, which form the inner lining of the intestine. These cells are particularly notable because colon cancer begins when cells in this tissue undergo changes that allow them to grow uncontrollably.

    The intestinal lining is constantly renewing itself. Older or damaged cells are replaced by newly introduced ones, making controlled cell division essential for keeping the digestive tract healthy. However, when the signals that regulate this process become disrupted, excessive growth can create opportunities for cancer to develop.

    In mice without IgA, the researchers identified changes in gene activity associated with cell proliferation, the process through which cells divide and increase in number. Crucially, these changes appeared before any tumors became visible, suggesting that the antibody helps regulate an early step in cancer development.

    "We assumed there must be some sort of receptor on the epithelial cells that was mediating this," Donaldson states.

    The researchers suspected that IgA was interacting with a specific molecular structure on the surface of intestinal cells, allowing it to influence how those cells behaved.

    Gabriella Lima dos Reis, the study's second author and a graduate student working in Gabriel Victora's laboratory, investigated a promising candidate called DMBT1.

    In a recent development, DMBT1 is a receptor found on the surface of epithelial cells that can bind to IgA. Previous research had connected it to several types of cancer, but scientists had not established precisely how it functions in the development of colon tumors.

    How Gut Bacteria and IgA Control Tumor Formation.

    Further experiments revealed that DMBT1 plays two very different roles depending on whether IgA is present.

    Sources indicate that when intestinal bacteria are present, DMBT1 activates signals that encourage epithelial cells to divide. This response is part of the normal activity of the intestinal lining, which must continually replace cells to maintain its protective barrier.

    Sources indicate that igA helps keep that growth under control. When the antibody binds to DMBT1, it restrains the receptor's activity, effectively acting as a brake on cell proliferation.

    It has been revealed that without IgA, however, DMBT1 signaling can continue without sufficient restraint. Intestinal cells then divide more rapidly than they should, increasing the likelihood that tumors will develop.

    In a recent development, the researchers confirmed that this excessive growth depends on several interacting factors. When gut bacteria were absent, DMBT1 signaling was disabled, or normal amounts of IgA were available, epithelial cell division remained under control.

    Together, these findings reveal how a common immune molecule helps maintain the delicate balance between necessary tissue renewal and potentially dangerous overgrowth.

    According to recent reports, "If IgA is missing, epithelial cells that are performing their normal function -- responding to bacteria by producing newly introduced cells -- can keep dividing unchecked, leading to cancer," Mucida notes. "We think this homeostatic effect is IgA's main function. This was a substantial surprise.".

    Recent findings suggest that homeostasis refers to the body's ability to maintain stable, healthy conditions despite constant changes in its environment. In this case, IgA appears to support that balance by preventing normal intestinal cell renewal from becoming excessive.

    A Fresh Possibility for Preventing Colon Cancer.

    By identifying DMBT1's normal role in intestinal cells, the Rockefeller team has uncovered a potential target for future colon cancer prevention strategies.

    Instead of waiting until a tumor develops and then attempting to destroy it, researchers may eventually be able to influence the biological signals that make tumors more likely to form.

    Sources indicate that "Based on the mechanism we discovered, perhaps we could influence epithelial cells to be less likely to develop into a tumor," Mucida says. "We know, for example, that having polyps increases your chances of getting colon cancer, so we think that there could be an opportunity to target this pathway after polyps are removed. Right now, there are no interventions available at that point.".

    Colon polyps are growths that develop along the inner lining of the large intestine. Although many are harmless, some can eventually become cancerous. Removing them during a colonoscopy can reduce cancer risk, but researchers are interested in finding additional ways to prevent future tumors from developing.

    The newly identified IgA and DMBT1 pathway could offer one such opportunity, although additional research is needed to determine whether targeting it would be effective and safe in humans.

    Could Beneficial Gut Bacteria Help Prevent Cancer?

    The discovery also raises another intriguing possibility. Certain intestinal bacteria may actively help protect against cancer by influencing how epithelial cells behave or by encouraging the production of protective antibodies.

    While much of the research into the gut microbiome and cancer has focused on harmful bacteria that promote tumor formation or accelerate cancer growth, some microbes may have the opposite effect.

    It has been revealed that "What is potentially even more exciting is that there is evidence that individual species of bacteria can have really specific effects on epithelial cells as well," Donaldson notes. "A lot of research has focused on bacteria that induce tumors or can exacerbate their growth, but we have some evidence that there are bacteria that could do the opposite, just as IgA does. To that end, perhaps we could develop a probiotic supplement that induces a protective IgA response. This is all very speculative, but it's one direction that we could look towards in the future.".

    In a recent development, such an approach would aim to use beneficial microorganisms to stimulate the body's existing protective mechanisms rather than directly attacking cancer cells. However, the idea remains speculative, and the mouse experiments do not establish that taking IgA supplements or probiotics can prevent colon cancer in people.

    It has been revealed that for now, the findings provide a clearer picture of how the immune system and gut microbiome cooperate to maintain healthy intestinal tissue. They also suggest that some of the body's most important defenses against cancer may operate long before the disease becomes detectable.

    Mucida adds, "Overall, there is a lot more to learn about how the dance between bacteria, antibodies, and epithelial cells in the gut works to maintain health.".

    Recent findings suggest that fnatic has confirmed the departure of its longest-serving player, jungler Razork, who is set to join Team Heretics. With support Lospa also set to leave, the London club faces a near-total LEC roster rebuild for 2027.

    Sources indicate that fnatic has made its first confirmed exit official as it rebuilds its LEC roster for 2027. Razork was the London club’s longest-serving player and its main playmaker. He leaves after five seasons in the jungle.

    Recent findings suggest that the club marked the departure with a farewell video titled “Thank You, Iván”. In it, Fnatic recalls him arriving as a young player with huge ambition.     Recent findings suggest that the rebuild runs deeper than the jungle. Every Fnatic team member except Lospa was due out of contract in 2026. The support was signed until the end of 2027.

    According to recent reports, that deal will not keep him at Fnatic either. Lospa has reportedly agreed verbally to join SK Gaming for 2027. No buyout is involved in moving his contract between the two clubs. With that move, the one contract running beyond 2026 also leaves the club.

    In the jungle, Yike is set to replace Razork in a 2027 line-up of Soboro, Yike, Vladi, Doggo and Labrov, according to Sheep Esports sources.

    The overhaul follows a difficult year. Fnatic finished eighth in LEC 2026 Versus. It then placed seventh in Spring, which ended on 10 May. Summer brought the same finishing position.

    Sources indicate that A loss to GIANTX on 30 August kept the team out of the Summer playoffs. That defeat left the club absent from Worlds for the first time since 2016.

    In a recent development, the developer hosted a livestream to celebrate, where it also debuted two new trailers: the launch trailer (below), as well as another look at gameplay. The gameplay trailer also indicates off more of the game’s Talos-2 world, and sets up the mystery at the centre of its narrative.

    If you’re going to be playing Endfield on PC, you’ll be happy to know that you can expert a breezy experience with support for 120fps. The game also comes with a wide range of modern technologies, including Nvidia DLSS Super Resolution, and Frame Generation. Both Xbox and PlayStation controllers are supported, too.

    #120874. 10 Games That Will Feel Better To Play After GTA 6

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1766 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

    10 Games That Will Feel Better To Play After GTA 6

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1766 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • If you're like 32.5 million other people around the world, you've probably been dedicating a huge amount of time to GTA 6 lately, and you can't imagine what your life will be like when the experience is over.
    • Sources indicate that all good things must come to an end, and eventually, your time in Leonida will reach a conclusion.
    • Titles like this one help you appreciate the craft of video game development more than ever, as they fully exploit many of the aspects that make the interactive industry the most special of all those focused on entertainment.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If you're like 32.5 million other people around the world, you've probably been dedicating a huge amount of time to GTA 6 lately, and you can't imagine what your life will be like when the experience is over.

    Sources indicate that all good things must come to an end, and eventually, your time in Leonida will reach a conclusion. However, crossing that frontier doesn't necessarily have to be a bittersweet farewell but rather an opportunity to re-evaluate everything that comes next.

    Titles like this one help you appreciate the craft of video game development more than ever, as they fully exploit many of the aspects that make the interactive industry the most special of all those focused on entertainment.

    Therefore, if these hypermodern times have already gotten to you and are making you nervous about what will come after Jason and Lucia's story, calm your anxiety by checking out this list of ten games that will feel better to play after GTA 6.

    If you're wondering how on earth this list is going to start with one of the games most diametrically opposed to the philosophy of GTA 6, like GRIS, the answer lies precisely in that statement.

    After an adventure brimming with stimuli, endless possibilities, lengthy explanations, and violence that ranges from the personal to the systemic, what better way to unwind than with one of the most focused and introspective titles ever conceived?

    In just three hours, without a single word and in a straightforward manner, GRIS takes you on a soothing path of reflection, making peace with the circumstances, and reveling in an audiovisual experience that engulfs you to the point of baptizing you with its art.

    Without bullets or socioeconomic problems that dictate your relationship with the law, but with platforms, elegance, and a creative intent so distinct that you won't be able to help but fall in love by the time the credits roll on the Sunday afternoon it takes to complete it.

    The cliché of "best game ever" versus "best game today" strikes me as both amusing and illogical, but I do believe there's some value in considering The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake in light of GTA 6.

    Both titles excel in their focus on player freedom, yet while GTA achieves this within a stunning range of action that opens up numerous possibilities, Ocarina of Time Remake does so in a much more concentrated and whimsical way.

    The charm lies not in the immeasurable variety of options, but in the immeasurable creativity of the single alternative they offer for each sequence, demonstrating in the process how the notion of agency has evolved over the last 30 years.

    They are two ends of the same spectrum, and experiencing the same sense of enjoyment through discovery in such different ways is what makes them complement each other far better than you might initially imagine.

    Having spent its entire existence in the shadow of Rockstar's work, returning to Saints Row 2 now that GTA has taken a 180-degree turn in its approach has become more fitting than ever.

    Jason and Lucia face a more realistic, weighty world with consequences, masterfully encouraging restraint and attention to detail, breaking the connection that pitted the two franchises against each other for so long.

    Hence, whether you're among those who didn't fully embrace the change in philosophy or those who did, Saints Row 2's humor and arcade style are a perfect fit to reduce the pleasurable cortisol rush produced by GTA 6.

    Don't get me wrong: I greatly appreciate Rockstar's courage in going against its own trend, though that doesn't mean I'm not much more eager to play a more relaxed game once I decide to stop wandering around Leonida, postponing saying goodbye.

    After GTA 6, it's quite clear the developer has mastered every imaginable variation of the driving genre, which includes the adrenaline-fueled and spectacular style they employed during the Midnight Club 3: DUB Edition era.

    The fact that the vehicles in their latest product had to prioritize accuracy and composure was necessary to fit the rest of the game's structure, yet the primal thrill of getting behind the wheel and flying at 300 kilometers per hour in the most improbable way possible was sacrificed.

    Consequently, even considering that the genre as a whole is today much closer to realistic simulation than arcade driving, dusting off your copy of Midnight Club 3: DUB Edition after GTA 6 would be in the instruction manual if GTA 6 had one.

    Neither approach is inherently better than the other, evidently, but the desire to truly revel in the speed instead of worrying about the cost of a crash will grow stronger on you with each passing second.

    Years go by, and it's incredible how no third-person shooter has understood that they are morally obligated to look to Vanquish to understand how to keep the genre from perpetually stagnating.

    Gunfights in GTA 6 are technically impressive and an absolute marvel in terms of action sequences, and yet there isn't a second that goes by that I don't think of Sam Gideon and the thunderous perfection of his combat performance.

    Instead of being a turn-based confrontation where both sides take turns behind a wall to exchange bullets, Vanquish is a spiral of destruction that doesn't even stop to reload, presenting a striking contrast to the game we're discussing here.

    In a recent development, would being able to slide at full speed and defeat giant robots in GTA 6 make sense? No. Am I dying to play through Vanquish for the thirtieth time for every occasion I have to stay put in cover? Absolutely.

    While this might sound utterly personal, few things please me as much as revisiting a developer's older games after a long time, which brings us to Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas.

    Being the franchise's installment I've sunk the most hours into and the reason I love open-world games, it creates an intrinsic incentive for GTA 6 because it allows you to appreciate the passage of time.

    Many of the gameplay concepts we enjoy in the franchise today, such as character customization, routines, and minigames, were pioneered by CJ, and taking a step back to appreciate what San Andreas did over 20 years ago is magical.

    This recommendation might be harder to justify theoretically because, generally speaking, GTA 6 is a vastly superior version, though the magic of nostalgia is something it won't acquire for another couple of decades, while San Andreas has plenty of that.

    Rockstar did an exceptional job, like few developers in history, of truly discouraging lethal attacks through a bloody, sensitive, and visceral presentation, though it's ironic that these same qualities are what elevate DOOM Eternal.

    Being careful with how you drive or which body parts you shoot is excellent, but I'd be lying if I didn't admit that a part of me misses the raw brutality with which you can manipulate the Doom Guy to commit hellish extermination.

    The two titles contrast sharply in both their approach to combat and the ease of movement that enables it, so just thinking about DOOM Eternal's levels, flying all over the place while leaping from execution to execution, makes my mouth water.

    Furthermore, being able to shoot an enemy entity in the face with a shotgun without being completely dismayed by my own lack of humanity is a significant bonus, because I do miss being able to disconnect from the consequences of my characters' actions.

    GTA 6 is a game of distance, in the sense that its experience focuses heavily on trajectories, the separation between spaces, and the distinct biomes, doing everything Yakuza 0 refuses to do despite also being an open world.

    Kamurocho and Sotenbori occupy a tiny fraction of Leonida's map, and there's no vehicle other than your own two feet to traverse them, though this allows you to connect with every back alley and building in a way that no other title has been able to instill in me.

    That familiarity and closeness with which Yakuza 0 relates to its inhabitants, locations, and activities is invaluable, and although GTA 6 manages to generate identical emotions, the difference in scale creates an impressive sense of belonging to Kiryu and Majima's journeys.

    There are many points of convergence, but the size breaks down the comparison, allowing their divergences to become apparent as the hours pass, thus highlighting the asymmetries that each offers to fans of the genre.

    It's clear after just a couple of hours of gameplay that Red Dead Redemption 2 is the primary influence on GTA 6, so we can all agree that we wouldn't be here if it weren't for Red Dead Redemption.

    Replacing the noise of neon lights and social media with horses and forests is something Arthur Morgan's game could easily do, but what even the legendary outlaw can't achieve is to also hark back to a time when even design was more contemplative.

    Unlike its sequel, Red Dead Redemption is a prototype whose full expression was prevented by technological limitations, resulting in a much quieter, more poetic, and simpler journey, but with the hints of grandeur that its direct and spiritual successor would achieve in 2018 and 2026, respectively.

    Therefore, riding back through its empty landscapes, conversing with its few interactive characters, and firing its limited guns is the handbrake for the Pegassi Vitello inside which we find ourselves in GTA 6, letting us breathe fresh air and appreciate the beauty of slower times.

    If at any point between 2013 and now you had told me that GTA 6 would be much more like Shenmue than any other video game, I would have thought you needed a psychiatrist, but here we are.

    If you're surprised by the attention to detail in drinking a beverage, observing the routines of dozens of NPCs, having to stay fit and healthy, or enjoying complex minigames, let me inform you that Yu Suzuki was already doing it all back in 1999.

    While Shenmue is more similar to Yakuza 0 in scale, it also resembles GTA 6 in that both embrace a life simulation design, where walking, talking, playing, interacting, and other such actions aren't driven by the sheer volume of fun but rather by the experience of placing yourself in someone else's shoes.

    That talent for immersing you in a reactive, living world that transcends your existence is reserved for the legends, and if you can tolerate the difference in technological advancement and size, Shenmue will easily show you why it feels like a great-great-grandfather of GTA 6.

    Scientists discover a fresh type of depression that common antidepressants struggle to treat

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (966 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A newly identified form of depression may help explain why some people struggle to find relief from commonly prescribed antidepressants.
    • In a recent development, the discovery emerged from an analysis of clinical and genetic information from more than 10,000 Australians with depression.
    • Circadian depression is associated with the body's 24-hour internal clock, which helps regulate when we feel awake and when we feel sleepy.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A newly identified form of depression may help explain why some people struggle to find relief from commonly prescribed antidepressants. Researchers at the University of Sydney have discovered a subtype called "circadian depression," which appears to be closely connected to the body's internal biological clock.

    In a recent development, the discovery emerged from an analysis of clinical and genetic information from more than 10,000 Australians with depression. Nearly one-quarter of the participants in the study, which focused on people with severe, recurrent or persistent depression, showed characteristics of this newly identified subtype.

    Circadian depression is associated with the body's 24-hour internal clock, which helps regulate when we feel awake and when we feel sleepy. People with this form of depression tend to respond less favorably to common serotonin-based antidepressants. However, treatments that target the brain circuits involved in controlling circadian rhythms, including melatonin, melatonin-targeted antidepressants and light therapy, may offer more effective options.

    Published in the British Journal of Psychiatry, the findings shed light on the genetic factors associated with this subtype and offer a possible explanation for why widely used medications such as SSRIs (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors) are less effective for some patients.

    A Hidden Type of Depression Affecting Nearly One in Four Patients Studied.

    To investigate the biological differences between forms of depression, researchers examined information collected through the nationwide Australian Genetics of Depression Study. Their analysis included clinical histories and genetic data from more than 10,000 people who had experienced depression.

    Industry observers note that the researchers identified nearly 25 percent (2,604 participants) as having circadian depression. Several recognizable patterns distinguished these individuals from other people with depression.

    According to recent reports, those with the circadian subtype were more likely to experience seasonal changes in their depression, sleep for longer periods when depressed, and wake up feeling exhausted despite spending more time in bed. They were also more likely to be night owls, meaning they naturally preferred staying awake late and waking later in the day.

    The differences extended beyond sleep patterns. Depression often began earlier in life for these individuals, and their symptoms tended to be more severe (such as mania and higher levels of suicidal thoughts). Genetic analysis also revealed an increased predisposition to inflammatory and cardiovascular health problems, along with major neurodevelopmental disorders, including ADHD.

    First author Dr. Emiliana Tonini from the University of Sydney's Brain and Mind Center said:.

    "Our research has identified circadian depression as a fresh subtype, affecting around a quarter of people in our study into those with severe, recurrent or persistent depression.

    "Depression is not a uniform illness, and understanding the characteristics of different subtypes means that we can give people earlier access to treatments that will be most effective for them.".

    Why Common Antidepressants May Be Less Effective.

    One of the most important implications of the discovery involves how depression is treated.

    Medications such as SSRIs and SNRIs (serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors) are generally among the first treatments offered to people diagnosed with depression. These drugs work by influencing chemical messengers in the brain that help regulate mood.

    However, the researchers found that these medications tend to be less effective for people with circadian depression. Individuals with this subtype also experience more side effects, suggesting that conventional antidepressants may not be the best initial approach for everyone.

    It has been revealed that because circadian depression is closely associated with the body's internal clock, therapies designed to influence that clock may be particularly useful. Light therapy, for example, uses controlled exposure to bright light to help regulate biological rhythms. Melatonin, a hormone involved in signaling when the body should prepare for sleep, and antidepressants that target melatonin pathways may also be relevant treatment options.

    Recent findings suggest that co-senior author Dr. Jacob Crouse from the Brain and Mind Center explained:.

    "Because circadian depression is linked to people's internal body clock, treatments targeting the circadian rhythm, such as light therapy and melatonin, may be much more relevant, and clinicians should reach for these much earlier in people with this presentation.

    "For those who find that antidepressants are not working for them, it is key to speak to your clinician for advice about your individual circumstances.".

    A Fresh Approach Could Improve Depression Treatment in Young People.

    Recognizing circadian depression earlier could be especially important for younger patients, who may otherwise spend valuable time trying medications that are less suited to their particular form of depression.

    Professor Ian Hickie, Co-Director of the Brain and Mind Centre and a clinical psychiatrist, warned that failing to identify this subtype in young people can contribute to unsuccessful early treatments and unnecessary side effects.

    The findings highlight the importance of recognizing that depression is not a single, uniform condition. Different biological mechanisms may contribute to similar symptoms, meaning that treatments effective for one person may provide much less benefit to another.

    By identifying patients whose depression is closely tied to circadian rhythms, clinicians may be able to offer more targeted treatments earlier rather than relying on the same initial medication approach for everyone.

    "We really want young people to receive the most appropriate treatment early in their course of illness.

    "Most young people will be offered SSRIs first up, but for at least a quarter there are better circadian-focused medical and behavioral options to help treat and manage their condition.".

    In a recent development, materials provided by University of Sydney. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that everything is Crab is a roguelite evolution game where you start off as a blob, needing to eat to upgrade yourself and learn to survive! There are some base-level stats that you can start with, sometimes making you a bit more than a blob, but you'll still need to come a long way if you want to survive in the harsh world around you.

    It has been revealed that the map itself is interesting, with areas of snow, rain, and desert. These areas can affect your blob, freezing you or slowing you down as you move through the sand. There are some foods along the ground in the form of fruits, but mainly you can beat up smaller creatures and bugs so that you can eat their flesh. This fills up a bar at the bottom of the screen that then allows you to evolve!

    Sources indicate that when you evolve, you can pick one of three upgrades that appear, some of which help you eat faster or ones that change the way you look physically, or ones that upgrade evolutions you have previously made. There are some that give you bigger attacks or change the way that you dash away. It's quite fun to see the combination that you end up with and how they all gel together. Though, these evolutions are worth reading through because sometimes they have less-than-desirable effects that pair with them.

    As you continue to grow and evolve in Everything is Crab, there is also a timeline on the top of the screen. This indicates moments when bosses will appear, who will trap you in a giant fenced area. You will then need to beat up this boss, as they will continue to chase you around until you've died. One giant spider guy actually started dropping web pods that released more spiders - it was quite the undertaking! Defeating bosses does give you DNA strips, which can be used to re-roll your evolutions or to upgrade your evolutions so that they do double the increase that you want to pick.

    Sources indicate that there are some areas that you can discover, represented by a question mark on your map. These little interaction points give you three options to choose from, primarily at tiny trees or at giant mushrooms, which change how you interact with mushrooms in other places on the map. There are also places where you can hide, though that wastes time!

    According to recent reports, slowly, through doing more and more of these runs, you will unlock new ways of playing, like different difficulties or starting points for your blob, which continue to make the game more interesting. I like the size and pacing of these runs, which do save, so you do not need to do them all at once. I do find that sometimes the UI overlaps itself on my mobile phone, which can be a little strange, but you are still able to read everything anyway.

    Sources indicate that download now! Everything is Crab.

    A significant part of the point of The Blood of Dawnwalker is that you're on a fixed time limit. You've got 30 in-game days and nights to try and save your family, and if you don't manage to see everything the game has to offer, well, the game's director is fine with that. But that doesn't matter as much now, as The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting its 1.2 update next week that adds in a newly introduced game plus mode.

    Industry observers note that "If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with New Game+!" a post from the devs explains. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over; the level cap will be raised to 100; enemies will be balanced and scale uniformly across all regions; and items will have NG+ versions with updated stats." Sounds like your usual new game plus affair! I suppose it is a good opportunity to try out different things compared to your first playthrough, but I'm not exactly aligned with the idea that the timer restriction is too restricting (as some mods have made clear how others feel that way).

    In any case, the update goes a tad further than that. If you got the Eclipse Edition of the game, the in-game soundtrack that came with it "will be extended with additional songs from the game." You can expect the soundtrack on streaming services soon, too. While details are slimmer here, there are also some planned balance changes, like updated enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat, and terrain geometry has seen some improvements to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration.".

    Overall, a bit of a smaller update compared to the last one, but one I'm sure will be welcome to some all the same. If you've not had a chance to check the game out yet and still feel on the fence about it, here's some lovely words from Mark's review: "There’s always that sense that something crucial or unexpected could be lurking around the next corner, to pull you into a quest dripping with depth and intrigue. It works to ensure the more busywork-esque tasks attached to angering Brencis and his Boyars never make Vale Sangora feel home to a string of boring boxes to tick. It’s a vibrant, constantly changing place with a thousand different threads metaphorically criss-crossing just beneath its surface, just as ancient ruins literally criss-cross beneath its swamps, crags, and forests.".

    • According to recent reports, battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending patch has been officially detailed.
    • Upgrade 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.
    • Industry observers note that patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller patch.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending patch has been officially detailed. The patch, version 1.1.3.5, arrives tomorrow, January 20 right when Season 1 was supposed to end. Part of the update’s goal is to extend the current season, until Season 2 kicks off in the middle of February.

    Upgrade 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.

    Industry observers note that patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller patch. When Battlefield Studios announced it earlier last week, the developer didn’t promise any major changes or fixes, so expectations never got out of hand.

    In a recent development, the patch is mainly made up of bug fixes, but it does have three key areas of improvements to gameplay. There’s a substantial focus on melee combat, how responsive/unresponsive it is with the various melee tools, and how melee behaviour interacts with sprinting and other animations.

    Recent findings suggest that the end result should be faster attack speeds for the knife, and clearer wind-up animations for both the knife and the sledgehammer. The timing dictating when melee damage gets credited has also been made more consistent in different environments.

    It has been revealed that interestingly, sprint is now only interrupted when the melee attack reaches its target. As it stands, sprinting is only interrupted after the full duration of the animation has been completed, which adds to the that perceived feeling of sluggishness.

    Recent findings suggest that the other major, and arguably most confusing is the nerf to jet cannons. The patch is going to make jets far less stronger against other air vehicles, requiring 40% more hits to destroy a target. This is puzzling because jets - and air vehicles in general - are already the least survivable in Battlefield 6.

    And, considering how the rest of a jet's arsenal is either situational or nearly ineffective, the cannons were really the one guaranteed way of downing other air vehicles, so long as you manage to land your shots consistently. While the change is wellmeaning, the percentage will likely be reduced in future patches.

    Finally, the enhancement makes a few refinements to UI across the game, though mainly aimed at Redsec and modes where players wear armor. Armor bar visibility has been improved, and there’s a fix for the annoying bug that sometimes caused the armor bar to disappear every few seconds.

    Read on below for the 1.1.3.5 change log.

    8 Things You Must Do Before Ending Chapter One in GTA 6

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that there is a lot that you can do in the first chapter of Grand Theft Auto 6.
    • After chapter one, everything in GTA 6 changes, and you don’t have the opportunity to get everything done that you might want to, so you want to be sure that you have a checklist and that you complete it before making your way to Vice City and starting bigger and better things.
    • Sources indicate that note: It is important to note that taking up Mattia’s offer will end the first chapter of the game.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that there is a lot that you can do in the first chapter of Grand Theft Auto 6. You can deep sea dive for treasure, hang out with friends, complete missions, set up for Lucia, and a lot more. However, some of this absolutely needs to be done before you hit the end of the first chapter.

    After chapter one, everything in GTA 6 changes, and you don’t have the opportunity to get everything done that you might want to, so you want to be sure that you have a checklist and that you complete it before making your way to Vice City and starting bigger and better things.

    Sources indicate that note: It is important to note that taking up Mattia’s offer will end the first chapter of the game. There will also be spoilers ahead about chapter one.

    Sources indicate that jason and Lucia have a chance to be madly in love in the beginning of the game. If you prepare for Lucia to get out of prison, work on Jason’s appearance, and focus on how they interact with each other, it will build a solid foundation.

    It has been revealed that there is a hard reset that comes at the end of the first chapter, and for a while, Lucia will be on her own while Jason recovers. With that being remarked, it will take a bit of a toll on their relationship.

    This means that if you raise it up very high in the beginning, you won’t need to worry about needing to rebuild it as much later in the game, saving you a bit of time later on.

    Industry observers note that immediately after setting up your BuckMe account, you are told that you need to start saving money. The first goal in the game is to have a total savings of $5,000 stashed away. This is a pretty easy goal to hit, especially since there are a fair number of money-making opportunities in the first chapter.

    You want to make sure that you hit this goal, as when the hard reset comes at the end of the chapter, you will lose everything except what is in your savings account.

    As an added bonus, putting money away into your savings account will also raise your relationship, so it is a win-win situation. After you have everything saved up, the rest of your money is stuff you can play with.

    Now that you have saved up the necessary cash for your family savings account, you might have some money burning a hole in your pocket. It is time to go on a bit of a shopping spree.

    As I mentioned, you won’t be able to take this money with you into chapter two, so you will want to spend all of it. Buy some clothes, and definitely upgrade your weapons.

    It has been revealed that there is no point in upgrading your car, as you will lose this after chapter one. Instead, focus on increasing your wardrobe and upgrading your weapons as these will carry over into the next chapter.

    There are some missions that you only have access to in the first chapter, and some of them belong to Shirley - Jason’s neighbor. She is a kind lady, and she will occasionally ask you to complete a few tasks.

    These consist of getting her some alcohol, and stealing a mobility scooter from a lady nearby. They are fun short missions that you can complete within a few minutes, but they are worth doing because they are quite fun.

    Recent findings suggest that don’t worry about the treasure hunting, as you will be able to come back to it later on. Only certain missions disappear after the first chapter.

    Industry observers note that there’s tons of details in GTA 6, which means that there are a bunch of collectibles that you can find scattered about. Some of these collectibles are books and magazines, and several of them are found around Jason’s house.

    According to recent reports, before you end chapter one, you will want to get the books around Jason’s house. These include one in the bedroom, two in the living room, a magazine on the back deck, and one in the shed. Each of these disappears after the first chapter.

    In a recent development, along with this, you will want to grab the sunglasses in Donny’s trailer. You will make your way over there during one of the missions in the first chapter, so you shouldn’t miss out on them, but make sure to pick them up while you have the chance.

    Industry observers note that if you have been focused on upgrading your weapons, gathering clothes, and putting money into your savings, then you will probably need some extra cash in the first chapter. Instead of searching for treasure, you should instead focus on completing the lost drug missions.

    It has been revealed that there are four lost drug missions around Key Lento and up to the Grassrivers. These are special missions that end up disappearing after chapter one ends, so you will not have the ability to go back and complete them later on.

    Since this is the only time you have access to them, you may as well complete them for the extra cash and spend it on stuff that will help you later in the game.

    Industry observers note that while I have already established that buying weapons is important because they carry over, it is also important to grab the unique weapons that are obtainable early in the game. There are a couple weapons that you can find around the islands in Key Lento, and they will carry you in later parts of the game.

    For instance, the Assassin Pistol can be found on a small dinghy on an island and it is great for completing missions stealthily in later parts of the game, and it has become one of my go-to weapons for staying hidden.

    According to recent reports, there is also a shotgun that you can find that is quite powerful. It gets outclassed by other unique weapons later on, but it is great to have in chapter two.

    One thing that is nice about GTA 6 is that it gives you the option to manually save. This means that you can create save points at key points in the game so that you can return to them later on.

    I highly recommend completing what you can in chapter one and then creating a save point right before you go to do the tourist trap mission, as this is the last mission of the chapter, and it is also the point of no return.

    If you want to play the game over but don’t want to deal with the slower pacing of the first chapter, you can skip all of that with a save right before the chapter change.
