    Industry News: Manufacturer of Heroes 3: Operation Torch Review

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1300 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that company of Heroes 3 has come a long way since its 2023 release, slowly making its way to the real-time strategy hall of fame after a rather rough start.
    • Industry observers note that upgrade 3.0 helped bring the game to its full potential, but mechanical polish only goes so far.
    • The dynamic campaign remains the highlight of Company of Heroes 3, but thanks to Operation Torch, the game finally has a scripted, story campaign that’s worth the trouble.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that company of Heroes 3 has come a long way since its 2023 release, slowly making its way to the real-time strategy hall of fame after a rather rough start. And yet, until now, something was missing.

    Industry observers note that upgrade 3.0 helped bring the game to its full potential, but mechanical polish only goes so far. Until recently, Company of Heroes 3 was a brilliant strategy game with strong mechanics that lend themselves well to single-player, but this was offset by a lack of quality content you could go through solo.

    The dynamic campaign remains the highlight of Company of Heroes 3, but thanks to Operation Torch, the game finally has a scripted, story campaign that’s worth the trouble.

    Sources indicate that operation Torch is the first single-player campaign DLC for Tech giant of Heroes 3. It was preceded by the unorthodox yet highly entertaining Final Stand tower defence DLC, but surviving wave after wave of German tanks is no substitute for a touching story.

    In that sense, the choice to depict Operation Torch is a poetic one. While American forces were being put through wringer in Pacific islands, the US had yet to launch any major land operations against the Germans and Italians.

    The North Africa landings sent a green Army against veteran enemies. The Americans turned out to be quite adept at learning on the job, but the lessons there were written in blood. As a DLC, Operation Torch is similar.

    Company of Heroes 3 emerges victorious once you see it through, but that success comes on the back of some blunders and failures that I hope are not repeated if or when Relic Entertainment decides another story-driven DLC is due.

    The DLC focuses on three American soldiers from the US Army’s 34th Infantry Division, all the way from the landings in Algeria to the crushing of Axis resistance in Tunisia.

    As far as individual story beats go, Operation Torch is adequate. Becker, Russo and Flanagan are likeable and quite distinct, and their commentary enhances the missions for the most part. There are some occasional immersion-breaking bits that strike out as silly, just about all of them relating to ‘tutorial’ speech.

    For example, in a rather late mission in the campaign, Becker instructs us to defend fuel points because “we need the fuel to build tanks.” Well yes, Colonel, in game we do, but I’m operating under the assumption that these tanks were manufactured in a plant somewhere in Detroit rather than spontaneously spawned through good vibes and virtual resources somewhere in Tunisia.

    This is nowhere near as egregious as in the much-maligned Rommel campaign that comes with the base game, but it would have been nice to have the option to disable tutorial-style objectives and commentary for people who are familiar with the game or who are going for a second playthrough.

    I need to emphasize repeat playthroughs here because, although Operation Torch is a linear, story-based DLC, it incorporates lessons from other Manufacturer of Heroes 3 releases that make it more replayable than other campaigns in a similar vein.

    Most missions are fairly open-ended in terms of how you can approach them. This is complemented by a decent degree of customization after each mission depending on how you accomplish both primary and secondary objectives. The Italy campaign had similar choices, but the Operation Torch system is closer to that of the Final Stand DLC.

    Sources indicate that the effects of the upgrades you pick are rather tangible. For example, early on, I managed to unlock M3 assault halftracks as a command call-in. Despite being rather underwhelming in their basic battle taxi configuration, these can be converted into game-changers.

    The Americans turned out to be quite adept at learning on the job, but the lessons there were written in blood.

    Many of my missions were saved because I was able to bring in an M3 converted into 75mm gun carriers that provided quick, on-call artillery support to break down defenses. When dug in myself, the M16 variant with the .50 quad-mounts made mince out of Axis infantry, allowing outnumbered defenders to hold out. All of this could have gone differently had I chosen another upgrade perk, which would have had its own advantages.

    Final Stand’s influence is particularly felt in those defensive scenarios, where its wave mechanics reach their zenith.

    Base game mechanics sometimes make these last stands slightly less dramatic than they could be at first, primarily because, as in real life, liberal application of engineering obstacles and overlapping fields of fire make incoming waves trivial. That false sense of safety comes apart spectacularly once heavier armor rolls in and you learn that Bazookas can’t dent it.

    Relic managed to craft missions that reward sound tactics. Generally speaking, if it works in real life, it will work here. There is one exception that deserves its own section, and that’s the abysmal commando raid mission.

    Sources indicate that when the Operation Torch announcement came about late last month, the commando gameplay was by far the most exciting part. I’ve been counting the days until SAS: Rogue Heroes comes back for its third season, and I was hoping the commando levels would be a good way to make the wait easier. I was sorely mistaken, I’m afraid.

    According to recent reports, the level where you plant explosive charges is an affront to modern game design, primarily because it is just… Pac-Man. With guns.

    In a recent development, you play one lonely commando, and your job is to slip by German patrols to plant demolition charges on 88mm guns. Every time you die (which, in my experience, is a lot), you respawn on the last checkpoint. Besides snipers, taking out any enemy does virtually nothing as they respawn almost immediately as well.

    The result is a level that’s both archaic and devoid of meaning. There’s no way to fail the mission, as you just keep sending more and more single commandos into the breech, the Germans reciprocate, and you’re sitting there playing Pac-Man timing patrol movement patterns for a dry 30 minutes.

    The mission is a one off, much like the American debacle in the Kasserine Pass in February 1943, but it leaves a mark on what’s otherwise a well-built campaign with strong design and balancing.

    Playing Operation Torch and the Italy campaign back-to-back has been great because you get to see how far Allied land operations in the Mediterranean Theater of Operations have come from the shaky landings in Algeria to the assault on Monte Cassino that opened the road to Rome.

    Recent findings suggest that it’s nice to see an oft-forgotten part of World War 2 history given the attention it deserves. The British and German versions of the fight for North Africa have been told a million times over, but with a few exceptions (most notably Call of Duty 2: Big Red One), the American African campaign is constantly overshadowed by later exploits in Europe and the Pacific.

    In a recent development, operation Torch also lays out a blueprint for potential future DLCs that focus on telling stories, rather than just adding new units to the same old multiplayer slog. The combined force of this DLC with update 3.0 released earlier this month puts Company of Heroes 3 in the spot it was always meant to occupy since its launch.

    Relic made a bold choice in depicting Operation Torch to this degree, and it paid off in spades. Firm of Heroes 3 mechanics come alive in a fight that doesn’t get the attention it deserves, in spite of occasional hiccups. The first narrative-driven DLC for the game reveals that there’s plenty of untapped potential in it, and it’s left me hoping more of them will come.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that while following a peculiar trail of silver and saffron leaves around the largest roots of the Treehouse, you come across a hexagonal wooden door lying half-hidden among ivy and moss. Scraping away the dirt, you discover a faint, absurd engraving of a newspaper. What mystery is here? You turn the brass knob – strange, it is warm! – and the engraving of the newspaper flutters. The pages turn faster and faster, emitting a howling gale that bowls you head over foot. When you pick yourself up, you are inside a vast attic full of books and bricabrac, lit from one side by windows that offer no view of the outside world – just light and mist.

    According to recent reports, tarnation! You have been lured into the eternal prison of Sunday Afternoon. Fortunately, there are several ways to escape. Each of the arcane objects before you is secretly a portal, transporting you to another site of arcane activity, in a bizarre web of diversions that cannot possibly reflect the hand of a human curator. Which will you choose?

    As you step forward, your toe nudges an ornamental scroll. It growls and wriggles like a panicking caterpillar, scooting away under a table. Before you lose sight of it, you discern the title and subject of the text – it's an essay by Kyle Tam about the yokai of Promise Mascot Agency.

    Deep in a drawer, you discover a sour-smelling binder full of extracts from an ancient and all but indecipherable dispute over the discovery of "generative AI" in something called "Significant Walk". The stakes are long-buried, but many of the individual pieces of writing are lively. Here is Bruno Dias noting in passing that "one of the harms of the 'AI' political project is the propaganda machine dedicated to making you feel stupid and helpless." Here is a professorial interjection from Brendan Keogh calling on the warring parties to recognise when "critiques of generative AI are actually just deflected critiques of the capitalist relations of technology and labour". Here is Mike Cook arguing that "what's happening is not unusual, it's not extreme, it's not unfair and it's not a 'public flogging'." Here is a ticker tape message from Hannah Nicklin observing that "if your radical position doesn’t have room for transformation it will not be safe until it contains just you".

    According to recent reports, A footnote in the same dusty sheaf of papers points you towards another work from Mike Cook in a different drawer. This one consists of neon slides, slotted into an antique View-Master, and explores a comparison between procedural generation and street photography.

    In a recent development, peering at the weirdly white and opaque windowpanes, you realise there are intricate equations traced in the condensation. It appears to be a post-mortem for a "post-cosy" game called Danchi Days, in which developer Melos Han-Tani discusses wishlist conversion rates and the problem of not fitting neatly into any recognisable genre.

    According to recent reports, A snowglobe stands on a mantelpiece, the flakes still orbiting a miniature washtub as though the object had been recently shaken, even though the chamber has clearly been abandoned for decades. You put it to your ear, anticipating the faint jingle of Xmas bells. Instead, you are almost deafened by a screeching guitar chord. Here is Erin Keane to explain.

    Next to the snowglobe on the mantelpiece, there's a souvenir shop conch shell, polished to a high sheen. You put that to your ear, hoping to catch the soothing shuffle of surf on shingle, and a disembodied voice tells you to piss off. Tim Sniffen has some thoughts about gentrification, and why only he should be allowed to do it.

    Again, one of these mystic artefacts hides the key to your release from the suffocating stillness of Sunday Afternoon. Which will you choose? Or have you, perhaps, brought a sorcerous teleportation device of your own? Please share. Here is Joanna Newsom's Cosmia to help you think.

    Though it may seem like we just had a significant life sim release in Heartopia, 2026 actually has more than one highly-anticipated release in that particular subgenre of cozy game. The next big one on the horizon is Starsand Island, the life and farming sim from Seed Sparkle Lab.

    Sources indicate that the game has been gaining momentum since the launch of a demo in October last year, but the developer never quite managed to commit to a date for its debut title. Until now.

    In a recent development, seed Sparkle Lab revealed today that Starsand Island will enter Early Access on February 11, which is only a bit over one week from now. This goes for Steam and the Xbox Preview Program version.

    The developer stated to expect a fairly short Early Access run, as the full launch is expected in the summer of this year. When the full release arrives, the game will also make the jump to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series, as well as Switch 2.

    The full release is also expected to bring Steam Deck support and introduce the multiplayer mode, which will not be available during Early Access.

    Recent findings suggest that starsand Island has something of a unique look compared to other games in the subgenre. The storybook, anime-inspired aesthetics are popular in the realm of gacha games, of course. However, seeing as this particular game isn’t gacha, being a premium product means it’s going to offer something free-to-play games aren’t designed to.

    Speaking of which, the game will be available in two editions: Standard and Deluxe, with the latter including Romanticism-inspired outfits, furniture, and other customisation items. If you buy either during launch, you’ll also get a Chinese New Year bonus with even more outfits and furniture.

    On top of the usual systems of farming, mining, and making friends with adorable characters (and animals), the game also has combat that pits you against ancient guardians. You can, of course, also build a home in it, and decorate it to your heart's content.

    Seed Sparkle Lab says you can expect about 100 hours of content in the Early Access launch build, and more features will arrive over the course of the next six or so months, including a crossover event with My Time At Portia.

    In a recent development, you can look forward to more Starsand Island coverage from us in the near future. Until then, you can get started by planning who you’re going to date now.

    Breaking: Scientists discover a surprising twist in how the body burns calories

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Unlike ordinary body fat, brown fat burns calories to generate heat, making it an attractive target for future obesity treatments.
    • In a recent development, while white fat primarily serves as an energy reserve, brown adipose tissue uses energy to keep the body warm.
    • In a recent development, exposure to cold naturally activates brown fat, prompting scientists to search for medications that could mimic this response.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Unlike ordinary body fat, brown fat burns calories to generate heat, making it an attractive target for future obesity treatments. Researchers at the University of Basel and University Hospital Basel have now investigated whether medication can switch on this energy-burning tissue in humans. Their surprising findings suggest that harnessing brown fat with drugs may be more challenging than anticipated.

    In a recent development, while white fat primarily serves as an energy reserve, brown adipose tissue uses energy to keep the body warm. People with more active brown fat also tend to be leaner and have better metabolic health.

    In a recent development, exposure to cold naturally activates brown fat, prompting scientists to search for medications that could mimic this response. A research team led by Professor Matthias Betz at the University of Basel and University Hospital Basel examined whether activating a specific receptor, known as the beta2 adrenergic receptor, could stimulate brown fat in humans. Their findings were published in the journal Cell Metabolism.

    Drug Boosts Calorie Burning Without Clear Brown Fat Activation.

    According to recent reports, to investigate, the researchers conducted two experiments involving 11 healthy volunteers. They compared the effects of mild cold exposure with those of fenoterol, a medication that stimulates beta2 adrenergic receptors. The scientists measured how much energy the participants expended and used PET/CT scans to monitor brown fat activity.

    Sources indicate that both interventions caused the body to burn more energy. However, the scans revealed an vital difference. Only cold exposure produced clear evidence of brown fat activation, with the tissue absorbing considerably more glucose than it did following fenoterol administration.

    "We were surprised that energy expenditure increased strongly with fenoterol even though we could not detect a comparable activation of brown fat," states Betz. "Our study shows that an increase in energy expenditure does not automatically mean that brown fat has been activated.".

    Industry observers note that exactly where the additional energy is being consumed remains a mystery. The researchers suspect that fenoterol may increase energy consumption in other tissues, potentially including skeletal muscle or white fat.

    Implications for Future Weight Loss Drugs.

    The findings also suggest that the biological mechanisms controlling brown fat in humans are more complex than previously thought. Analysis of human tissue indicates that fully activating brown fat may require the combined action of multiple receptors or biological signals rather than stimulating a single receptor.

    Understanding these mechanisms could open upcoming possibilities for treating obesity. Current weight loss medications work by reducing appetite. However, as people shed pounds, their bodies often compensate by burning fewer calories.

    A treatment that simultaneously reduces appetite and increases calorie burning could help counteract this metabolic adaptation.

    Sources indicate that "Ideally, we could combine a reduction in appetite with an increase in energy expenditure," indicates Betz. "But first we need a better understanding of how brown adipose tissue is regulated.".

    It has been revealed that materials provided by University of Basel. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

    #120827. Why Do I Want To Paint The Walls In Grand Theft Auto VI?

    Why Do I Want To Paint The Walls In Grand Theft Auto VI?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (541 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing are on regular rotation in my home on my family’s screens, but not my own.
    • According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto VI is not a cozy game, but it has a substantial amount of cozy elements and mechanics.
    • And for some reason, I couldn’t start that process fast enough.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    I admire the cozy sim genre. Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing are on regular rotation in my home on my family’s screens, but not my own. In an odd way, I find the genre stressful, arguably the opposite of its intended purpose. I will happily and cathartically guide Grace Ashcroft through the tense hallways of Rhodes Hill in Resident Evil Requiem, but Pokémon Pokopia’s seemingly endless list of to-dos makes me sweat. It’s just not my genre, and I have come to terms with that.

    According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto VI is not a cozy game, but it has a substantial amount of cozy elements and mechanics. Bird (and animal) watching, for example, is apparent and encouraged early in the experience. You can also fix up your somewhat dilapidated home from almost the moment you are let loose outside of the opening tutorial missions.

    And for some reason, I couldn’t start that process fast enough.

    According to recent reports, I climbed to the roof to fix the leak and replaced all the stairs leading up to the home before I ever participated in the game’s namesake and stole a car. Normally, it’s the kind of interaction I skip or choose not to engage with, given the option. Or, I do the bare minimum to progress. Sure, I have all the options in the world to build and decorate a house and make it my own, but… that feels like a lot of work. And I am not an artist.

    The “cozy” elements of Grand Theft Auto VI are admittedly different from those in a game like Pokopia or Animal Crossing. You’re not designing your home (though you can pick a paint color), but it feels similar, and I am trying to figure out why I enjoy it here as opposed to other games. Is it because Jason and Lucia are so instantly believable as human beings that I want their home to be nicer?

    In a recent development, after some thought, I think it might just come down to Grand Theft Auto VI’s consistently impressive visual fidelity. Replacing the shingles on the roof, for example, offers a close-up look at Jason’s character model, and you can practically feel the texture of the asphalt while the heat of the sun beats down.

    According to recent reports, I don’t have confirmation, but it also just feels like someone at Rockstar did exhaustive research on what the process of replacing a roof shingle should look like, even if, I’m sure, it probably doesn’t quite work that way in the real world. Jason makes it look incredibly easy, to the point that it had me questioning if I should be climbing up to my own roof and taking care of some loose shingles myself. And you know what is a lot of fun? Watching someone who is good at something do the thing they’re good at.

    I’m now into the driving and shooting part of the game (and enjoying that, too!), but I am shocked at how grateful I was to have the option to stay home and put up drywall.

    According to recent reports, bad signal or dead zones? Download your complications before you leave and read anywhere.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    After a couple of years of regular testing behind closed doors, Cyberpunk 2077 multiplayer mod CyberMP is now out in open beta, giving anyone who fancies a bit of multi-merc action a chance to give it a go. Though, if you do, be prepared for bugs and crashes, as work on the mod is far from over with the release of this "true beta".

    According to recent reports, as shown off in the video above, CyberMP's not about being able to play through the base game's missions with friends, but rather cruise around Night City as a gang getting into races and PvP shootouts. In that regard, it seems more akin to GTA 4's online mode than GTA 5's, with classic improvised hijinks the main draw over being able to pull off gigs with a crew. Though, there do also look to be roleplaying servers which could scratch the itch of those more interested in pretending to be a merc than blowing up other people's rides.

    "After almost six years of development, countless reworks, and code rewrites, we're finally launching the public beta," the modders wrote on Discord. "Anyone can jump in and play now — no invites or applications needed. Fair warning: this is a true beta. Crashes, desyncs, and server drops under heavy load are completely normal for now. That's exactly why we need testers. We welcome everyone: regular players, future server admins, and those who just love breaking game mechanics.".

    Industry observers note that "Right now, our absolute priority is stability and fixing crashes," they continued later in the post. "Newly introduced features are planned, but we need to polish the foundation first. A huge thank you to everyone who has been with us since the early versions, helped with closed testing, and patiently waited. We've finally reached this milestone. Let's see how the project handles real player traffic!".

    Industry observers note that according to the modders, CyberMP's "client doesn't have a digital signature yet", which could cause antivirus software not to be a fan of it. They're also anticipating "problems with the anti‑cheat system", so it may be worth holding off on giving the mod a go if you're not keen on being trolled by someone with the sort of destructive power usually reserved for megacorps and AIs from beyond the blackwall in the Cyberpunkverse.

    Sources indicate that for info on how to get CyberMP up and running, as well as create a custom server dedicated to the likes of roleplay or races, head over to its website. As you might expect, the mod requires a legit copy of Cyberpunk bought on either Steam, GOG, or the Epic store.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It sounds like Koei Tecmo’s decision to finally release a Nioh game on PC day-and-date with PlayStation has paid off. The highly-anticipated Nioh 3 has gone live across both platforms, a first for a series that typically spends its initial release months as a console exclusive.

    On Steam, and despite having only been available for just a few hours, the game has broken series records, and it continues to climb.

    At the time of writing, Nioh 3 has peaked at 42,822 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), and the number keeps going up. Because it’s in the middle of day in Europe and everyone is at work, it’s entirely possible - if not likely - that this figure will get much higher. A weekend bump is also possible, as we’ve seen with several recent releases.

    As it stands, the current peak concurrent is enough to get the game in Steam’s top 20 most played games.

    In a recent development, this already puts it ahead of all other Nioh games on Steam. The original Nioh peaked at 10,649 when it released in November, 2017. Nioh 2 fared much better, peaking at 41,325 concurrent players in February, 2021.

    It has been revealed that of course, you could see that success coming a mile away. The game is currently number one worldwide in Steam’s list of top sellers. This is a jump of 46 positions, for a total of three weeks Nioh 3 has spent in that list.

    Sources indicate that there are many reasons as to why Nioh 3 has done as well as it has. Word of mouth coming off last year’s PS5-exclusive demo, and the more positive coverage that followed since are just two.

    Just last week, Team Ninja released a pretty generous demo across both platforms, which has been well received by players, and likely contributed to sales, in no small part because progress in the demo carries over to the full game.

    Recent findings suggest that critical reviews have been incredibly positive, too. We awarded the game four out of five stars, calling it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.” It will be interesting to see what number the highest peak concurrent actually settles on over the weekend.

    In a recent development, until then, if you’re jumping in yourself, our Nioh 3 guides are essential reading. Start off with these useful and actually informative gameplay tips, and don’t start playing until you’ve changed these settings. Once you’re ready to get deeper, be sure to read up on how to play co-op with other players, and how to summon AI Acolytes to help you out.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that EA Sports has worked with John Motson’s family to bring his iconic commentary to the hit sports game, EA Sports FC 27, as a digital tribute.
    • Industry observers note that motson passed away in February 2023 at the age of 77 and was the main commentator for BBC Sport for 50 years.
    • The voice of football will return in EA Sports FC 27 in the next game upgrade for all players to use if they wish to do so.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that EA Sports has worked with John Motson’s family to bring his iconic commentary to the hit sports game, EA Sports FC 27, as a digital tribute. If you don’t know the name, you will definitely recognize the voice, even if you aren’t a die-hard football fan.

    Industry observers note that motson passed away in February 2023 at the age of 77 and was the main commentator for BBC Sport for 50 years. He commented on over 2,500 games and 20 international tournaments on television and radio during his tenure. Motson starred in the same role for the FIFA video game series as its first commentator from FIFA 1996 to FIFA 2006, and also made an appearance in FIFA 19.

    The voice of football will return in EA Sports FC 27 in the next game upgrade for all players to use if they wish to do so.

    With permission from Motson’s widow and his son, his voice will return as the first late commentator to appear in the series. According to the BBC, EA paid Motson's family for the rights to use his likeness and recreate his voice, but the company would not disclose the financial terms of the deal.

    Sources indicate that fred Motson, the son of John Motson, told the BBC it "means an awful lot" to have his dad's voice in EA Sports FC once again. "I grew up with FIFA," he said. "I always used to tell my parents that I needed the latest console for Christmas because otherwise dad couldn't see how the game worked.".

    Mat Prior, Senior Game Design Director at EA Sports FC, told the BBC, "There was no way we would have moved forward with this in any way, shape or form if they weren't fully on board.".

    Motson’s voice will return using a combination of old recording sessions and generative AI. Prior explained that Motson's commentary in EA Sports FC 27 was constructed using old lines he recorded over the years and AI. He mentioned it’s "the only way" to make it happen, since recordings don’t exist of Motson speaking about and mentioning the names of modern players.

    However, EA assures that the use of AI to recreate Motson’s voice won’t become commonplace. "It's not there to replace commentators in any way, shape or form... there's certainly no future intends to replace anyone with AI," said Prior.

    "From a gaming standpoint, it's something we've used for many years - like machine learning to help drive animation systems and so on and so forth," outlined Prior.

    The style of football commentary is unique to each individual, and every fan has their favorites. The little quips, tone, and moments of laughter make the voices feel natural, responsive, and immersive, something AI is unable to replicate.

    EA assures that the use of AI to recreate Motson’s voice won’t become commonplace.

    John Motson’s tribute arrives in Title Upgrade v1.3.0 on 26 November 2026 as an optional commentary, alongside the existing selection of broadcast teams.

    It has been revealed that also on its way with Title Revision v1.3.0 is further gameplay tuning based on player feedback, including dribbling balancing adjustments, foul call improvements, and interception recovery tweaks. Moreover, you can expect updates to matchmaking and Amps functionality in The Grounds, along with quality-of-life improvements in Manager and Player Career.

    #120820. World’s largest trial of robotic knee replacement reveals surprising results

    World’s largest trial of robotic knee replacement reveals surprising results

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1276 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that robotic technology can help surgeons perform knee replacement operations with greater precision, but that accuracy does not necessarily translate into better results for patients.
    • According to recent reports, robotic technology is becoming increasingly common in knee replacement surgery around the world.
    • The UK-wide RACER-Knee trial was funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) in partnership with Stryker, the manufacturer of the robotic equipment evaluated in the study.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that robotic technology can help surgeons perform knee replacement operations with greater precision, but that accuracy does not necessarily translate into better results for patients. The RACER-Knee trial, the world's largest clinical study of its kind, found that patients who underwent robot-assisted knee replacement experienced similar levels of pain, mobility, and recovery to those who received conventional surgery. The findings provide notable evidence about the use of robotics in health care and highlight where future technological developments and research could make a difference. Coordinated by the University of Warwick and University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire (UHCW) NHS Trust, the trial was published in The Lancet, the world's oldest and one of its best-known general medical journals.

    According to recent reports, robotic technology is becoming increasingly common in knee replacement surgery around the world. It is now used in 6% of procedures in the UK, 16% in the US, and 42% in Australia. The technology is designed to help surgeons position artificial knee joints more accurately and customize procedures to suit each patient's anatomy.

    The UK-wide RACER-Knee trial was funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) in partnership with Stryker, the manufacturer of the robotic equipment evaluated in the study. The Warwick Clinical Trials Unit, UHCW NHS Trust, and the Royal Orthopaedic Hospital in Birmingham led the research. It represents the world's largest double-blinded, randomized controlled trial comparing traditional total knee replacement with procedures performed using the Stryker Mako robotic system, the most widely used system of its kind worldwide.

    Greater Precision Does Not Improve Recovery.

    Recent findings suggest that twelve months after surgery, patients in both groups reported comparable recovery, mobility, and pain levels. Although the robotic system enabled surgeons to operate with greater precision, patients did not experience measurable improvements in their overall outcomes during the first year. The researchers also found no increased risk of serious adverse events associated with robotic assistance, suggesting that it was as safe as conventional surgery.

    The trial was jointly led by two chief investigators in the UK.

    It has been revealed that professor Andrew Metcalfe, of Warwick Medical School at the University of Warwick and a consultant orthopedic surgeon at UHCW NHS Trust, remarked: "We are delighted to have completed this world-leading randomized trial of an exciting technology that is now being used globally and at scale. It is an important step in the process of innovation and will stimulate lots more high-quality studies. We are very grateful for the support of the many patients who took part which is so important, but also the NIHR and Stryker for working so well together to support this critical study. Technology such as this could really help the care we give for patients, but for robotic-assisted knee replacements, there is still work to do before we see benefits such as less pain or better movement.".

    Professor Edward Davis, a consultant orthopedic surgeon at The Royal Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Foundation Trust and honorary professor at the University of Birmingham, said: "The trial demonstrates robotic-arm-assistance allows for higher precision, and in theory the system should allow surgeons to customize the procedure according to a patient's anatomy. These results are by no means a condemnation of the robotic systems, but more understanding of the ideal position for a knee replacement and personalization for each patient is needed. We'll then be able to truly take advantage of the advanced precision of robotic systems.".

    According to recent reports, professor Anthony Gordon, director of the NIHR Health Technology Assessment (HTA) Programme, noted: "Innovation in healthcare depends on evaluating promising technologies rigorously and at scale. While this study shows robotic-assisted knee replacement is not yet improving patient outcomes, it highlights opportunities to refine these technologies and harness their precision to deliver better care in the future. The NIHR continues to fund robust studies, such as RACER, ensuring we learn how to deliver the latest technologies most effectively within the NHS.".

    How Robotic Knee Replacement Works.

    It has been revealed that total knee replacement is among the most frequently performed elective surgical procedures worldwide for people with knee arthritis. During traditional surgery, orthopedic surgeons use standard surgical instruments and rely on their training and experience to position the artificial joint.

    Robotic technology offers an alternative approach in which the surgeon controls a robotic arm during the operation. The system helps position surgical instruments with exceptional accuracy and allows surgeons to adjust the angles and depths of their cuts with greater flexibility. These capabilities make it possible to customize procedures to individual anatomy in ways that are not achievable with conventional techniques.

    Landmark Trial Finds Similar Patient Outcomes.

    Industry observers note that the study involved 339 patients treated by 33 surgeons at 10 hospitals across the UK. Despite the potential advantages of robotic technology, researchers found no meaningful difference between the two groups in the trial's primary outcome measure, the Forgotten Joint Score, one year after surgery.

    It has been revealed that this assessment measures how conscious patients are of their artificial joint while carrying out everyday activities. Ideally, a successful knee replacement allows patients to go about their daily lives without frequently noticing the artificial joint. Patients achieved similar scores regardless of which surgical technique was used.

    Other measures also showed comparable results. These included walking ability, pain during hospitalization, pain during the first three months of recovery and at 12 months, and the likelihood of requiring another operation.

    Researchers initiative to monitor participants for ten years to determine whether differences between the two surgical approaches emerge over a longer period. One particularly crucial question is whether robotic assistance reduces the number of patients who eventually need additional knee surgery.

    Robotic Knee Surgery Takes Longer and Costs More.

    Operations performed with robotic assistance required additional time (on average 10.5 minutes) and cost approximately £950 more per procedure.

    Although the robotic system improved surgical precision, it was not associated with a higher risk of serious adverse events, indicating that the procedure appeared to be as safe as traditional knee replacement.

    However, when assessed against current NHS spending thresholds, the robotic technology evaluated in the trial was not considered cost-effective during the first year following surgery.

    The Future of Personalized Knee Replacement.

    The researchers believe that robotic technology could become more valuable if surgeons learn how to use its enhanced precision to better accommodate differences in individual patients' anatomy.

    According to recent reports, determining the ideal placement of an artificial knee joint for each patient could eventually allow surgeons to turn greater technical accuracy into meaningful improvements in recovery, pain relief, and mobility. Achieving those benefits will require further technological development and additional research, making personalized robotic surgery a promising area for future investigation.

    The findings of the RACER-Knee trial were published in The Lancet.

    According to recent reports, the research was organized by University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire NHS Trust and the University of Warwick. Funding was provided by the UK NHS research organization, the National Institute for Health Research, through its Health Technology Assessment Programme (NIHR128768).

    Stryker, the manufacturer that manufactures the robotic system, covered the additional expenses associated with performing robotic surgery during the trial. The company did not participate in analyzing or interpreting the study results.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Just one day after Marvel dropped the final trailer, a latest international teaser for Avengers: Doomsday has arrived, giving us another look at Robert Downey Jr.'s villain.

    Sources indicate that the teaser, which was originally shared by Disney Korea but has since been posted on Twitter by ScreenRant, opens with Doctor Doom delivering his coldest line yet. "You call yourselves heroes? Avengers, Fantastic Four, X-Men? You shall all kneel before Doom." The rest of the clip contains shots of Marvel heroes Johnny Storm, Thing, and Thor showing off their powers, before the Fantastic Four, the Wakandans, and Shang-Chi meet up in what looks like Steve Rogers' retro house. Watch the full video below.

    The Disney Korea account has shared a upcoming Avengers: Doomsday international trailer! Watch Here 👇 https://t.co/nZ9grAnKkdNovember 24, 2026.

    Industry observers note that however, the most interesting part comes right at the end, where we see Thor and Steve Rogers visit Doom Castle, where Doctor Doom sits on the throne. What could the duo be doing walking right into the villain's lair? This seemingly supports the fan theory that Doom may be pretending to be an ally to the Avengers early on in the film.

    More evidence arrived in the new Doomsday trailer, where fans pointed out that someone seems to be edited out of the Fantastic Four lineup when the group goes to visit Steve Rogers at his house. We already know that Doom has been collecting Marvel heroes ahead of Doomsday, starting with kidnapping Hulk during the Endgame Encore added footage. Also, during the VisionQuest finale, we learn that Doom has already resurrected Scarlett Witch, and seemingly made her one of his Latverian Witches.

    Industry observers note that so, could Doom be pouring poison into Rogers' and Thor's ears? Alas, the upcoming scene could just be the pair visiting the villain to try and reason with him, as we can guess from the synopsis, the baddie is set to do a lot of damage in the new movie. There is also the issue of Steve Rogers flipping between timelines. We know that Doom has a personal vendetta against the Avengers due to the multiversal damage they caused at the end of Avengers: Endgame when Steve went back in time to be with Peggy after returning the Infinity Stones. Perhaps Steve is visiting Doom Castle to make amends.

    All will be revealed when Avengers: Doomsday hits cinemas on December 18, and December 16 in the UK. For more, check out our guide to the Marvel timeline, and keep up with upcoming Marvel movies and reveals on the way.

    • In a recent development, "Nobody was hurt" in a shooting last week near the California office of Clockwork Revolution developers InXile, both the studio and local police have confirmed.
    • "Officers got there [on November 11th]," Tustin police sergeant Christopher Peterson remarked in statement to Aftermath.
    • "We’re relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office," a spokesperson for InXile noted in a separate statement.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, "Nobody was hurt" in a shooting last week near the California office of Clockwork Revolution developers InXile, both the studio and local police have confirmed. The incident, which took place on November 11th, is right now being investigated and police have reportedly taken a suspect into custody.

    "Officers got there [on November 11th]," Tustin police sergeant Christopher Peterson remarked in statement to Aftermath. "They responded to a report of a drive-by shooting there. Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt. Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why.".

    "We’re relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office," a spokesperson for InXile noted in a separate statement. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate.".

    Recent findings suggest that inXile are set to release steampunk RPG Clockwork Revolution next year. The studio, developers of the likes of Wasteland 3 and The Bard's Tale IV, are one of the few Xbox-owned studios not to have been affected - at least as of writing - by Microsoft's ongoing mass layoffs this year.

    Since being announced in 2023, Clockwork Revolution's dripped with Bioshock-ish vibes and popped up semi-regularly at Xbox showcases. "Wield the power of an incredible device to travel back in time, changing the past and rewriting the future of the city you call home: the vibrant steampunk metropolis of Avalon," reads its Steam synopsis. "In this immersive RPG, you'll step into the shoes of Morgan Vanette, a fully customizable player-character and member of the Rotten Row Hooligans. Travel between past and present as you battle the ruthless Lady Ironwood, who has been manipulating time to keep the working class struggling while amassing immense wealth and power.".

    Best wishes to the staff at InXile, here's hoping that going forwards they're able to get with making what's looking to be an intriguingly funky game without enduring any more concerning incidents like this one.

    Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.0 brings a new world, and a Fortnite collaboration

    📅 06 Feb 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (860 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vg247

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that hoYoverse just wrapped up a big Honkai: Star Rail Special Program.
    • According to recent reports, the upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason.
    • Planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that hoYoverse just wrapped up a big Honkai: Star Rail Special Program. We’ve been waiting for this one for a couple of weeks now thanks to a delay, but the developer has finally delivered all the news on Version 4.0, which will arrive February 13.

    According to recent reports, the upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the massive latest world headlining Version 4.0.

    Planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

    In a recent development, the squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

    The imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

    The Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

    Much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

    As you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

    Sources indicate that version 4.0 introduces two latest 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

    Recent findings suggest that general Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

    Her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

    The other latest arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

    Industry observers note that when you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

    She also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

    Version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

    Recent findings suggest that finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the fresh outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

    According to recent reports, if you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be confirmed at a later date.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that if you're a longtime reader, you may remember the launch of Torerowa, the Dark & Darker-like multiplayer dungeon crawler, back in 2025. And since then, it's been chugging along quite nicely, having now reached its 15th season! But what else could Torerowa have in store? Quite a lot, it seems.

    Season 15 of Torerowa debuts today and includes many fresh layers to the dungeon, bringing the total depth to floor B35F. That means more loot, more monsters and more risk, but even more potential rewards too. However, that's just the tip of the iceberg, as this enhancement also sees the introduction of Guilds!

    Speaking of socialising, there's also newly introduced places to visit in the form of the Adventurers' Tavern and the Workshop, the former of which is sure to be a big favourite with players, especially if you've played Dark & Darker and enjoyed the antics in the pre-match tavern lobby.

    Outside of this new content, there's also plenty of intriguing, smaller additions such as the Treasure and Dress-Up Gachas, not to mention auto-translation for chat. All in all, it's a set of very exciting additions to Torerowa which, especially with Dark & Darker seemingly slipping out of the spotlight, makes this a great option for Tarkov-like dungeon crawling on mobile.

    But if you'd prefer a more small-scale, personal journey in a fantasy world, then we can provide that too. Check out our list of the best RPGs on Android to see some of our choice picks which you can play right now!

    In a recent development, GOC Esports took the opening map, but Revenant XSpark won the next two to reach the upper semi-final of the VCT Pacific Kickoff South Asia qualifier playoffs. Kryon Esports are next, with two South Asian places in the Pacific Last Chance Qualifier at stake.

    The third upper-bracket quarter-final of the VCT Pacific Kickoff: South Asia – Qualifier 2027 needed a deciding third map.

    Sunset ran for 51 minutes. Revenant XSpark levelled by winning Haven 13-5 in 35 minutes. They then won the deciding map, which lasted 49 minutes.

    The scoreline matches the two sides’ Predator League India semi-final, which Revenant XSpark also won 2-1. GOC lost the third-place match of that event to GodLike Esports. GOC now drop into the lower bracket and face RANKERS in the first lower round on Wednesday 25 November.

    Kryon booked their place in the upper semi-final by beating RANKERS 2-1. On the other side of the upper bracket, GodLike Esports beat Trigger Point Esports 2-0 and SIGN Esports beat Zexar Esports by the same score.

    Industry observers note that second place in that Predator League event earned Kryon 125,000 INR, while the winners collected 250,000 INR, VLR.gg reported. Both teams qualified for the APAC Predator League 2027, an offline event in Ho Chi Minh City.

    Revenant XSpark played the Predator League with Lightningfast, hellff, Hoax, deecee and Venka. Rinsat, now listed on Revenant XSpark’s roster alongside Hoax, Techno, venka, k1ngkappa and Madelyn, appeared in Kryon’s lineup for that event.

    Industry observers note that riot Games and JioBLAST are running the playoffs online as an eight-team double-elimination bracket from 23 to 29 November. The field came through an online Open Qualifier of 152 teams, held from 17 to 20 November. Revenant XSpark finished in the top four there, while GOC placed in the 5th–8th group.

    The South Asian qualifiers will be joined at the Last Chance Qualifier by one team from Oceania and the runner-up of the SEA Kickoff Playoffs. ONE Up is organising that event with Riot Games.

    Industry observers note that beyond it lies the 2027 Pacific Kickoff in Bangkok, from 11 to 31 January 2027. It will feature 12 teams: eight partner teams and four Open teams. The top three qualify for the first Masters event, Masters Seoul. Any Open team that reaches Kickoff receives a fixed US$100,000 per event on top of any prize money.

    The winner of Thursday’s match plays in the upper final on 27 November, and the grand final is on 29 November.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Heartopia has officially shared initial details about its first-ever collaboration event. The game, which rolled out a month ago to great success on mobile, as well as Steam on PC, has already been a staple among fans of Animal Crossing and The Sims.

    Things are kicking into gear, it seems, because the game is already about to host its first collaboration event, and it is with My Little Pony.

    Industry observers note that the Heartopia X My Little Pony event officially begins on February 14, but a pre-launch login event is now live through the actual collaboration’s start. The limited-time event offers players sign-in puzzles every day that will unlock time-limited Exhibition Passes.

    The first actual piece of My Little Pony-themed content can be yours if you complete all puzzles, as that gets you a limited edition costume for your pet, based on the show’s Spike. The event itself, which will be available until March 15, brings My Little Pony’s Tree of Harmony into the world of Heartopia.

    It has been revealed that the ponies need your help to Wield Elements of Harmony so they can reawaken the tree, and bring it back to Equestria. In gameplay terms, you’re going to want to perform daily sensing at the tree in order to earn three of the six Elements of Harmony: Honesty, Generosity, Loyalty, Kindness, Laughter, and Magic.

    According to recent reports, the more you do this, the more the tree’s Energy goes up, and the more rewards and resources you stand to earn. Even more time-limited Exhibition Passes, and Moonlight Crystals can be earned as you water the tree.

    In a recent development, badge Pull Tokens are your big reward, which is what you’re actually going to use to get the special Pony Series badges. You’ll earn ten time-limited Exhibition Passes each time you complete one of the three sets of Pony Series badges. Collect all three and you’ll earn Town Collaboration Series badges.

    Sources indicate that heartopia is a free-to-play game, so you know there is a Gacha component to this event. Expect six non-replacement Gacha Pools that each map to one member of My Little Pony’s Mane Six. Within each pool, you’ll be able to earn five outfit pieces, and one vehicle.

    Recent findings suggest that we also recently updated our guides on how to catch Frostspore fish - and if you’re into cooking, how to obtain every recipe and variant. If you haven’t already, definitely see if you missed any of these Heartopia codes, too.

    Sources indicate that the Grand Theft Auto 6 map is massive - big enough to fit multiple maps from previous games inside of it. With a map that big, there are bound to be a lot of hidden details. If you’ve been exploring Leonida, you may have found some of them.

    However, you probably haven’t discovered many of the hidden secrets this upcoming location has to offer. There are hidden missions and interactions that might blow your mind.

    In a recent development, for instance, have you discovered the alien hidden within the bunker? Maybe you haven’t been out to sea yet to find the kraken. There’s plenty to discover in this strange area.

    Deep in Pelican Valley, you can find an abandoned research center. This is the strange part; that comes when you are inside. The strange part is that when you step inside, you will get assaulted by a giant crab, which is something straight out of a horror movie.

    This is a great easter egg in GTA 6, that connects the game to a movie from the 1980s called Island Claws. In this movie, a scientist breeds giant crabs, and then everything goes completely wrong.

    Well, a scientist in GTA 6 tried doing the same thing, and it ended up breeding a giant crab that killed everyone, and now it is coming for you.

    According to recent reports, once you have made your way to the Starlet Motel in Kelly County, head northwest. Locate the abandoned car with the flashing lights. From here, follow the path into the woods and you will discover a lady being abducted by a UFO. It is a wild sight.

    Recent findings suggest that A few days later, go to sleep as the character you were playing as when you found the UFO. This will trigger a dream sequence where you need to sneak around alien eggs. It also gives you a look at the universe.

    Industry observers note that the whole dream sequence ends with you inserting a serum into a computer. I don’t want to give too much away, but it gets wild and there are cows involved.

    According to recent reports, there is a strange case that takes you to an alternate dimension in GTA 6. In reality, it seems more like it makes you trip extremely hard, but either way it is out of this world. It all starts by going to a construction site in Millport.

    Inside one of the shipping containers here, you will find a mysterious case that you can interact with, though the name of the item is listed as “???.”.

    From here, get ready to be sent on a wild trip where you need to do a lot of parkour. You basically walk through various shipping containers and reach an area where you must parkour your way to victory. It isn’t just parkour, as you will need to swim at certain points, but it is a trip you won’t forget.

    After you have completed the alien abduction event and had one of the weirdest dreams of your life, it is time to rescue an alien from an underground bunker. Once the dream sequence is done, head to Mariana County, just south of Hamlet.

    Industry observers note that here, you can find an old secret base. You will need to break in and climb down the ladder to get inside. Type in the code, access the building, and follow the corridors like you did in your dream.

    You will need to put in sequences and everything, but in the end, you will be rewarded by seeing a real alien, and you can even help it escape the base so that it can return home.

    Industry observers note that you may have spotted Skunkape during one of the earlier missions in GTA 6. During your time in Grassrivers, you can spot a creature running across the road. If you choose to follow it, it will disappear, and you may be wondering where it went.

    Well, if you continue your search, you can find effigies that look similar to Bigfoot, but this is not Bigfoot. It is another creature known as Skunkape. When you turn away from the effigy, you will get hit from behind, and a cutscene will play.

    After you have this encounter, you can go to Skeeter’s Bar in Hamlet and begin a mission for someone who is looking for the Skunkape. It is something you definitely don’t want to miss.

    Industry observers note that in Grand Theft Auto 5, you could get stuck out in the ocean, and it would require you to swim for a long time to get back to shore. It was very inconvenient, and so players probably aren’t very interested in getting stuck out at sea in GTA 6.

    According to recent reports, well, if you decide to go far out into the ocean and wait for a while, you will get rescued by a dog that is driving a jet ski. It is quite odd, but an amazing interaction that you can certainly miss if you never go out of your way to be stranded in the ocean.

    It has been revealed that the dog will also bring you to an island where there are other dogs, and it will also dig up some treasure for you. At least you don’t go home empty handed for all this work.

    Industry observers note that you can go searching for treasure in many different locations around Leonida. One of the best places is deep in the ocean, as you can find gold doubloons and more. However, there are some treasures around the map that come straight from space.

    Recent findings suggest that if you search around Mount Kalaga, you can find what appears as purple mist. This is an impact crater, and it is one of the few sites where you can find a meteorite that has crashed into the ground.

    While a space rock is cool, the best part about it is that you can sell it for a fair amount of money, so you will want to keep it on your person and take it to a pawn shop to get rid of it.

    In a recent development, something that the game doesn’t tell you is that there are cocaine flamingos, which is a term I never thought I would write, but welcome to GTA 6. There are 125 cocaine flamingos scattered around Leonida, and you need at least 100 of them to complete a task.

    You can go the entire game without realizing these statues exist, but if you pay attention, you will notice that these lawn ornaments are different from the standard ones found in many lawns.

    Recent findings suggest that instead of having the standard black and yellow beak, cocaine flamingos have a black and white beak. These flamingo ornaments can be destroyed to find bricks of cocaine that you can sell to a dealer.

    Industry observers note that there are many different strange finds that you can discover under the surface of the ocean. Treasures galore wait for you in the deep, but so do monsters. Thankfully, they aren’t alive, unless you count a shark as a monster.

    To the southeast of Gloriana Key, you can find a shipwreck. However, this is no ordinary shipwreck, as it was destroyed by none other than the mythical beast known as The Kraken.

    The Kraken’s tentacles are wrapped all around the ship, which reminds me of Pirates of the Caribbean. Keep in mind that you need to swim very deep to find this hidden secret, and it may take a while to spot thanks to how dark the ocean can be.

    There is a hotel that is run by The Kingfishers in GTA 6, but they unfortunately aren’t having a great day. This hotel is located in Pelican Bay, and you want to be careful when you go here, as there is a tiger.

    According to recent reports, when you approach the hotel room, you will hear gunshots. If you make your way over to the area, you will see a massacre, as a tiger is loose around the area and is eating the various gang members.

    It is a crazy interaction that is never marked on your map until you are nearby, so make sure you search the entirety of Pelican Bay and don’t miss anything.

    Capcom is shutting down online dinosaur shooter Exoprimal next year, 4 years after it first released

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (459 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Gamesradar

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Capcom has declared that its dinosaur shooter Exoprimal will be unplayable next September as the servers are being taken offline.
    • While not quite as massive as the year it had in 2026, Capcom's 2023 was incredible, with Resident Evil 4 and Street Fighter 6 releasing as two certified game of the year contenders and as two of the all-time greats in their respective genres.
    • Sources indicate that it had a bit of a cult following, but Capcom has announced it'll be joining the pile of dead live service titles next year.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Capcom has declared that its dinosaur shooter Exoprimal will be unplayable next September as the servers are being taken offline.

    While not quite as massive as the year it had in 2026, Capcom's 2023 was incredible, with Resident Evil 4 and Street Fighter 6 releasing as two certified game of the year contenders and as two of the all-time greats in their respective genres. But there was another, namely Exoprimal, a PvPvE shooter where you took a ton of Overwatch-like character classes into brawls where you'd fend off armies of dinosaurs.

    Sources indicate that it had a bit of a cult following, but Capcom has announced it'll be joining the pile of dead live service titles next year. In a post on the Exoprimal website, Capcom confirms that services for the game will go offline on September 29, 2027, with the post reading, "We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years, and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement.".

    As it begins the shutdown process, the game's survival pass premium tiers (aka, the paid battle pass) have been removed from the in-game store already. The game itself will be taken off sale on March 30, 2027, and those who own it will have six more months to play it before it's gone forever. With no way to access the content in single-player, it'll sadly join the ever-growing list of games that are just gone, which certainly isn't a bad omen for the all-digital future.

    Recent findings suggest that exoprimal was perhaps best known for being the bane of many a Dino Crisis fan upon its announcement – especially when there's a character who looks like that game's heroine Regina, who featured heavily in marketing. It was genuinely a fun time when you got into it, but it suffered from the same fate many live services do, that being there's too damn many of them, so it never really took off. It also didn't help that Exoprimal's best content was hidden behind a ton of playtime.

    Dino Crisis is more than "Resident Evil with dinosaurs" – it shaped survival horror as we know it.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A hacker has pleaded guilty to a number of online crimes, including the 2022 breach of Rockstar Games which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net.
    • The BBC report that, on November 16th, Arion Kurtaj pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar Games hack and a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17.
    • Kurtaj carried out the 2022 Rockstar hack while on bail for other hacking offences and being housed at a Travelodge hotel under police protection, the latter on account of rival hackers threatening to attack him over stolen Bitcoin stashes.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A hacker has pleaded guilty to a number of online crimes, including the 2022 breach of Rockstar Games which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net.

    The BBC report that, on November 16th, Arion Kurtaj pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar Games hack and a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17. Kurtaj, now aged 21, was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital indefinitely due to the severity of his autism, but was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial. He'll be sentenced at a later date.

    Kurtaj carried out the 2022 Rockstar hack while on bail for other hacking offences and being housed at a Travelodge hotel under police protection, the latter on account of rival hackers threatening to attack him over stolen Bitcoin stashes. The Rockstar hack was reportedly done using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into the hotel room's TV, plus a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.

    Sources indicate that 90 clips of unfinished GTA 6 were flung online by that hack, with Rockstar having refused to cooperate with Kurtaj's demand via an internal Slack channel that the tech giant contact him on massaging app Telegram within 24 hours. Rockstar claimed the breach cost them $5m million to recover from, in addition to staff having to waste thousands of hours.

    It has been revealed that earlier this year, GTA 6 suffered yet another leak, with a hacker or hackers going by "Cyberleek" posting various videos of the game in action. Rockstar and parent organization Take-Two promptly sprung into action, taking down videos, filing subpoenas, and issuing a statement that called the leak "heartbreaking".

    It has been revealed that hopefully with the game's console release later this week, those will be the only two GTA 6 leaks which have to be added to the annals of gaming history. As much as marketing can leave a bad taste in the mouth, especially when it barely shows anything of the actual product being advertised, neither of the GTA 6 leaks served much of a purpose beyond forcing people to waste some time and energy talking about the perpetrators.

    • Sources indicate that this is where Auto Drive comes in.
    • In a recent development, first, you must select a destination.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Grand Theft Auto VI is a game where you spend a lot of time behind the wheel. Always has been. But sometimes, you just won't feel like actively driving, but you also don't to waste money on a cab.

    Sources indicate that this is where Auto Drive comes in. It lets the game take over and drive you where you need to go in real time and all with a cinematic camera that shifts and moves, letting you take in the environment without all that pesky "having to pay attention to the road." Red Dead Redemption 2 had the same feature, and I have fond memories of taking advantage of it to watch Arthur ride his horse through that game's incredible environment. It's a great option in GTAVI, but how to use it and turn it on isn't immediately apparent.

    In a recent development, first, you must select a destination. Get the GPS set up to direct you to where you want to go.

    In a recent development, next, start driving. The Auto Drive is smart, but doesn't seem to be smart enough to make three-point turns or back out of parking lots. You need to be on your way before you can turn it on.

    Once you're on the path, hold down in the d-pad and press start to activate Cinematic.

    According to recent reports, once you've done this you should be able to hold down the Circle button on PlayStation or the B button on Xbox to activate Auto Drive and... voilà! You can sit back and let Jason or Lucia take the wheel. They will drive legally, even stopping at lights, but you can speed them up if they're taking too long.

    I've always enjoyed driving in Grand Theft Auto, but I was grateful to find this almost-hidden option early in the game.

    Sources indicate that nioh 3 has had a massive weekend on Steam, the type of launch you just don’t often see for Koei Tecmo games. Indeed, this has very clearly been a monumentous release for both the publisher, and developer Team Ninja.

    It is also, quite visibly, the most popular Nioh release ever on PC, and it was impressive watching more and more players jump into the game over the weekend and push the numbers higher.

    Nioh 3 came out swinging, breaking the series’ Steam concurrent player record immediately after lanch, with 42,822. Anyone keeping up with how well the game has been received, and how much it’s been anticipated by series fans and Soulslike players, would’ve told you that it was only the beginning.

    Late on Friday, and several times on Saturday, the game continued achieving new records, setting new peak concurrent levels every couple of hours. It happened again on Sunday, when the game finally settled on its current 88,045 peak concurrent (via SteamDB).

    Recent findings suggest that that’s an incredibly healthy player base, but more than that, it’s more than double the previous record holder, Nioh 2, which peaked at 41,325 concurrent players in 2021. Steam players appear to be very happy with the game, too, with over 1,560 reviews and an overall Very Positive rating.

    In Fishing Inc, you, well, fish. No surprises there.     And, to be honest, Reber may not have been far off. Fishing games have always been popular, combining the excitement of increasingly bigger catches while also being surprisingly laid-back.     Coming packed with a huge variety of species to catch, locations to visit and plenty of upgrades to hunt, Fishing Inc looks to be a perfect newly introduced addition to the catalogue of any fishing enthusiast on mobile!
